msgBody.Event_Description:
Jday 002 1934z

JCO providers have indications of 3 separate photometric changes on TJS-3, 43874. The first is observed at from -97 to -91 phase angle and is dimmer by about 1 vis mag. The second is from solar phase angle -89 to -85 and is brighter by about 0.5 vis mag. The third change is observed from -20 to 15 solar phase angle and is brighter about 1.2 vis mag and has oscillated between dimming and brightening over the last 4 days (Jday 363 to 002). The purpose of these changes is unknown and attached is a neighborhood of nearby satellites. Of interest of these is TJS-10, 58204 which is parked near TJS-3 at a distance of approx. 316 km. Analysis is ongoing.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
JDAY 363 1700z

JCO providers have indications that the photometric signature on TJS-3 (43874) has returned to its previously established pattern. The 1 visual magnitude change between -110 and -100 solar phase angle is no longer present as of JCO providers' collection on JDay 393. There have been no significant changes to the neighborhood, though the proximity to TJS-10 is still notable. 

Jday 361 1501z

JCO providers have indications of a photometric change in the early phase angle of TJS-3, 43874, where it appeared brighter by approx. 1 visual magnitude between -110 and -100 solar phase angle. The reason for the photometric change is unknown and a neighborhood of nearby satellites is attached. Notable from the neighborhood is TJS-3 and TJS-10, 58204, are parked within 300 km of each other and plane matched. Analysis is ongoing.

27 Dec: PSRA found indications this launch will now occur on 10 Jan at 0200 UTC. https://nextspaceflight.com/launches/details/7129

When the launch was advertised last month, it listed 17 December as the launch time. Dongfang Space signed an agreement for the Yinli-1 to launch 5x Jilin-1 Gaofen satellites, but it is unknown if those payloads will be on this initial launch of the rocket. https://twitter.com/raz_liu/status/1732382717873176958 https://forum.nasaspaceflight.com/index.php?topic=57734.0#msg2549410

JDay 016 1949z:

JCO providers have detected a photometric change on TJS-3 (43874).  The change occurred between the solar phase angles of -20 and 10 degrees. The satellite is in GEO with orbital characteristics of current GEO longitude of 172.92 deg E and an arrested drift rate. msgBody.Remarks:
17 Jan:  TZ-7 launched on time (14:27:30.728 UTC exactly). Docking will occur three hours after launch at approx 1727 UTC.  TZ-5 actually used the even faster 2 hours approach profile (actual time to docking 2 hours 7 minutes). This is the first one to use the just-slightly-longer 3 hours one. https://twitter.com/Cosmic_Penguin/status/1747633017420415161, https://forum.nasaspaceflight.com/index.php?topic=59908.60

***************************************

16 Jan: The final all-systems rehearsal for China's Tianzhou-7 cargo spacecraft launch mission was completed on Monday. The vessel, weighing 13.5 tonnes, will dock autonomously with the Chinese space station approximately 3 hours after launch.(1727 UTC, 17 Jan). https://twitter.com/HenriKenhmann/status/1747262889772339622, https://forum.nasaspaceflight.com/index.php?topic=59908.20

SUMMARY: JDay 019 0400z

JCO providers have verified a maneuver on SY-12 02 (50322) occurring at 1203z.
The satellite maneuvered from 139.7deg E longitude with a delta v of 0.135m/s, the effect of which was an increase eastward drift rate of 0.02deg E/day to 0.54 deg E/day.  Neighborhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver.

=================================================================

JDay 018 1915z:

JCO providers have verified a maneuver occurring at 1316z on 18 Jan, and a photometry change on SY-12 02 (50322).
The satellite maneuvered from 139.2deg E longitude with a delta v of 0.21m/s, the effect of which was an decrease in period of 10.7s and an increase in eastward drift rate of 0.05 deg/day to 0.557deg E/day. Neighborhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver.

The photometric change occurred between the solar phase angles of 5 degrees and 12 degrees. During this change SY-12 02 (50322) appeared to be 0.7 visual magnitude dimmer, reverting the change from 17Jan that was in response to the close approach with SBIRS GEO 6 (USA 336) (53355). The satellite is in GEO with orbital characteristics of 139.75 Deg E.

==================================================================

JCO providers have detected a possible photometric change on SY-12 02 (50322).  This change occurred between the solar phase angles of 5 degrees and 11 degrees. The purpose of the photometric change appears to be in conjunction with a close approach with SBIRS GEO 6 (USA 336) (53355), with a TCA time of 17Jan1511z with a minimum distance of 76.4 km.  During this timeframe 50322 had good lighting of 53355.  The satellite is in GEO and is currently at 139.15 E Longitude drifting eastward 0.5 deg/day.  Potential in-plane satellite neighborhood is attached for further upcoming close approaches.  Analysis is ongoing.

As of JDAY 022 0400z

JCO providers have indicated a possible upcoming launch of a Kinetica-1 from Jiuquan, China occurring on 23 Jan between 0352z and 0416z with an expected launch time of 0405z, carrying the following five expected payloads: 

Beijing Huanbao-1  | Taijing-1 03 |  Taijing-2 04 |  Taijing-3 02 | Taijing-4 03

Based on current information the satellite's orbit is likely to be LEO with orbital characteristics of 94.503 degrees inclination and 84.7480 degrees RAAN at ~500km( based on the assumption that the insertion orbit will align with satellites from the same predicted family.)
Potential in-plane satellite neighbourhood attached as a product. 

JCO is currently unable to provide commercial observations after confirmation of Launch. 18SDS will be the final determination for LEO insertions. 
Please check the public catalogue for details

JDAY 128 0508z:

JCO providers have indications of successful maiden launch of a LM-6C from Taiyuan, PRC occurring at 0321z, carrying multiple payloads; the Haiwangxing-01, Zhixing-1C, Kuanfu Guanfxue, and Goafen Shiping .  JCO providers have given one nominal for the four expected payloads. Based on current information the satellites are likely to be LEO with orbital characteristics of ~97.45 degrees inclination, and ~202.55  degrees RAAN.  Potential in-plane satellite neighborhood updated and attached as a product. 

JCO is currently unable to provide commercial observations after confirmation of Launch as a result tracking details will not become available. 18SDS will be the final determination for LEO insertions. Please check the public catalog for details.

JDay 128 0330z:

JCO providers have indicated a possible upcoming launch of a possible LM-6A or LM-6C from Taiyuan, China occurring between 7May from 0313z to 0355z with an expected Launch time of 7May 0320z, carrying a Neptune-1. Based on current information the satellite is likely to be LEO with orbital characteristics of an Inc of 97.4 degs and a RAAN of 202.31 degs.  Potential in-plane satellite neighborhood attached as a product. 

JCO is currently unable to provide commercial observations after confirmation of Launch. 18SDS will be the final determination for LEO insertions. Please check the public catalog for details"

JCO providers have detected a possible Photometric change on Shiyan 12 02 (50322).  This change occurred between the solar phase angles of -10 to -44 degrees. During this change 50322 appeared to be ~1.5 visual magnitude brighter.  The purpose of the photometric change is unknown but it appears to have reverted back to previous pattern of life. The satellite is in GEO at 131.82 deg E long and drifting 0.63 W deg/day. Potential in-plane satellite neighborhood is attached.  Analysis is ongoing.

msgBody.Follow_Up_Assessment:
As of JDAY 171 at 1919z:

SWF: Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, Shiyan 12 01 (50321) is a Chinese space environment exploration and related technology tests satellite, however, it is suspected that it is actually a military test satellite.  This photometric change occurred between the solar phase angles of -25 degrees and 5 degrees. During this change 50321 appeared to be 1.3 visual magnitude dimmer. The purpose of the photometric change is unknown however this change did occur while in close approach with USA 270 (41744) with a miss distance of less then 100km . The satellite is in GEO at 125.8 deg E long and drifting 0.64E deg/day.

SWF:  Based on available PAIR data, there are indications of a launch of a Ceres-1S from the Yellow Sea, China occurring on 26JUN24 between 0512z and 0557z. The launch is likely to take the payload into a sun-synchronous orbit. The payload for this launch is unknown at this time but it is speculated to be three Yunyao-1 15/16/17 which are new meteorological remote sensing and observation satellites.

msgBody.Remarks:
Mission Summary: Luch 5X (OLYMP K-2) is a Russian geostationary satellite built for the Russian Ministry of Defense and the Russian intelligence agency, FSB. While the purpose of the satellites has not been officially disclosed, the satellites are believed to serve two purposes. The first purpose is to conduct signals intelligence (SIGINT) and the second is to provide secure communications lines for governmental use. The Luch designation, which is also used to refer to the Russian Satellite Data Relay Network (SDRN), hints at the satellites being used in a data relay role.
Sourced by: PSM

msgBody.Follow_Up_Assessment:

msgBody.Email_Subject: NOTSO - Verified Maneuver / 58172 / COSMOS 2571 / NE - 3177_02Aug-1643Z - TACREP Notification
msgBody.Follow_Up_Assessment:
As of JDAY 215 at 1530z:

SWF: Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, COSMOS 2571 (58172) previously conducted some close approach ops with OBJECT D (58248) in December 2023 before boosting and maintaining a coplanar orbit at a much different height; resulting in periodic radial flybys with both objects.
A series of maneuvers in May and June 2024 changed the flyby cadence; now the objects are very co-orbital and co-planar but have a separated nodal crossing resulting in more of a "standoff" orbital set.

The specifics of the maneuver are:
--Time of Maneuver: 0922z on 31Jul2024 JDAY 213
--Delta V: 5.3781m/s
--Period Change:  -12.2816s
--Apogee Change: -13.9825km
--Perigee Change: -5.2975km
--Inclination Change: -0.0008deg
--Current Drift Rate: 0deg/day

2 58172  67.1508 152.7527 0010521 164.2939 321.8252 13.97203889    12
msgBody.Remarks:
Kosmos-2571 is a subsatellite that was released from Kosmos-2570, a Lotos-S SIGINT satellite with a passive ELINT payload, on 30 October 2023. The purpose of the subsatellite remains open to speculation. One possibility is that it also has an ELINT payload that uses a multi-position geolocation method to determine the position of radio-emitting sources on the ground, possibly to locate targets for electronic warfare satellites. In late November 2023, Kosmos-2571 released or separated from another object, "Object D".

msgBody.Event_Description:
As of JDAY 215 at 1530z:

JCO providers have verified a maneuver on Cosmos 2571 (58172) occurring at 0922z on 31Jul2024 JDAY 213.  This maneuver synchronizes orbit size metrics with 58428, OBJECT D (from the same launch on 27 Oct 2023) after 8 months of separation. The objects are on opposite sides of the earth but now in a fairly identical orbit.

The satellite maneuvered from 157.77deg RAAN with a Delta V of 5.38m/s, the effect of which was a RAAN change to 152.74deg, and a change in period of -12.28 seconds.
Neighborhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver.

The believed payloads are the first launch for the Qianfan (G60) Megaconstellation. It is understood that this launch will have 18 satellites and, based on current information, the satellites are likely to be injected into a LEO with orbital characteristics of:
88.5deg Inc and 350.9deg RAAN at an altitude of 1,160 km. 
Potential in-plane satellite neighborhood is attached as a product.

msgBody.Follow_Up_Assessment:
As of JDAY 219 at 0856z:

Based on available PAIR data, China performed a successful launch of a batch of 18 Qianfan telecommunication satellites that are part of the G60 megaconstellation. It is the first batch of an array of more than 14 000 satellites which is said having a purpose to compete with US Starlink megaconstellation.
The final altitude of these satellites is still not known at the moment but we have the following hypothesis : 

If the final altitude is around 520km : 

Rotated launch nominal to August 6 2024 (JD219) at 0644z:

The actual final launch will be released in a future NOTSO.

They reportedly provide the Ku-band communication and feature advanced multiple steerable spot beam antenna technology to enable ground users to communicate while on the move as well as secured uplink transmission for satellite antenna control. Mission Summary: Shijian-20 (SJ-20) is a Chinese experimental GEO satellite based on the new DFH-5 Bus, equipped with more than a dozen internationally leading technology verification payloads. msgBody.Remarks:
Mission Summary:
China claims the SJ-17 is an experimental satellite used to run communication and broadcast services as well as observe space debris. On 21 Apr 2021, Gen Dickinson (Commander of USSPACECOM) confirmed that the "SJ-17 is Chinese satellite with a robotic arm" and that Space-based robotic arm technology "could be used in a future system to grab other satellites." It is believed to be used for on-orbit space situational awareness (SSA) and close-up inspections. Its activities are consistent with the demonstration of RPO technologies for the purpose of satellite servicing and inspection.
Sourced by: TAB

msgBody.Follow_Up_Assessment:
As of JDAY 221 at 0040z,

SWF: Based on available PAIR data, there was a probable upper stage debris issue with the launch. S4S and space-track.org both reported that there has been a breakup of this rocket and further analysis is ongoing to understand the full magnitude of this event.

This is the first launch of China's Qianfan (G60) Megaconstellation which intended to be a starlink-like communications constellation.

======================================================================

As of Jday 219 at 1642z:

Based on available PAIR data, China performed a successful launch of a batch of 18 Qianfan telecommunication satellites that are part of the G60 megaconstellation. It is the first batch of an array of more than 14 000 satellites which is said having a purpose to compete with US Starlink megaconstellation. JCO Providers are currently tracking what appears to be 3 objects consistent with this launch, it is likely they will detect more objects as they deploy and separate.

msgBody.Remarks:
8 Aug 2024 0221z

The LM-6A upper stage appears to have a space debris problem. The 6 August 2024 launch was the 7th launch of the LM-6A and debris creation from the upper stage has been reported on at least 4 of them including this latest launch (launches 2, 5, 6 and 7 have had reports of debris from the upper stage). It is not clear whether this is from passivation of the upper stage or insulation breakup or other. Some debris breakups did not lead to additional objects reported in space-track.org causing speculation that the debris cloud is comprised of small pieces in those cases. This latest launch appears to be following a debris pattern seen on the two previous launches.  (Further detail in attachment).

msgBody.Remarks:
Gaofen 13, an improved version of Gaofen 4 is a Chinese civilian remote sensing satellite for the state-sponsored program CHEOS (China High resolution Earth Observation System). There is speculation as to the military purpose of the Gaofen-13 which China reports as 'wild' speculation. Possible Chinese military applications include identifying and tracking U.S. Strike Carrier Group activities, particularly in the SCS. There is also speculation as to the possibly missile warning purpose of the satellite. The Gaofen-13 is suspected to be an improved version of the Gaofen-4 satellite with significantly larger optical systems.

msgBody.Remarks:
Mission Summary:
China claims the SJ-17 is an experimental satellite used to run communication and broadcast services as well as observe space debris. On 21 Apr 2021, Gen Dickinson (Commander of USSPACECOM) confirmed that the "SJ-17 is Chinese satellite with a robotic arm" and that Space-based robotic arm technology "could be used in a future system to grab other satellites." It is believed to be used for on-orbit space situational awareness (SSA) and close-up inspections. Its activities are consistent with the demonstration of RPO technologies for the purpose of satellite servicing and inspection.
Sourced by: TAB

Mission Summary:
Fengyun-2F is a Chinese weather satellite and part of the Fengyun 2 meterological satellite series.   The satellite collects real-time weather imagery every 15 minutes for forecasters in China and neighboring countries.  It carries instruments for visible and IR high-resolution cloud imagery and for monitoring space weather.

As of JDAY 240 at 1330z:

JCO providers have detected a possible maneuver on Fengyun-2F (38049) occurring the 27th of August at approximately 02:56z.
The satellite was located at 111.73 deg E longitude, drifting at -0.04/day. Initial solves of the maneuver show an approximate 300s period change, and an increase in westward drift rate. This out of pattern, large orbit raise has been seen on previous Fengyun satellites as they begin to maneuver to the graveyard belt.

Potential in-plane satellite neighborhood is attached.
Analysis is ongoing.

As of JDAY 240 at 1650z:

JCO providers have verified a maneuver on Fengyun 2F (38049) occurring  on 27 Aug (JDAY 240). The satellite maneuvered from 111.73 deg E longitude with a delta v of 4.06m/s, the effect of which was an increase in westerly drift of 1.3 deg/day, a period of +303 minutes, apogee of +191 km and perigee of +6 km. Neighborhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver. 

A second maneuver has been detected and analysis is on-going.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

As of JDAY 240 at 1330z:

JCO providers have detected a possible maneuver on Fengyun-2F (38049) occurring the 27th of August at approximately 02:56z.
The satellite was located at 111.73 deg E longitude, drifting at -0.04/day. Initial solves of the maneuver show an approximate 300s period change, and an increase in westward drift rate. This out of pattern, large orbit raise has been seen on previous Fengyun satellites as they begin to maneuver to the graveyard belt.

Potential in-plane satellite neighborhood is attached.
Analysis is ongoing.

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, Fengyun 2F (38049), a Chinese weather satellite with IR high-resolution cloud imagery performed two manoeuvres. --Period Change: 626 secs

Fengyun-2F is a Chinese weather satellite and part of the Fengyun 2 meterological satellite series.   The satellite collects real-time weather imagery every 15 minutes for forecasters in China and neighboring countries.  It carries instruments for visible and IR high-resolution cloud imagery and for monitoring space weather.

msgBody.Event_Description:
As of JDAY 241 at 0115z:

JCO providers have verified two maneuvers on Fengyun 2F (38049) occurring on 27 Aug 24  (JDAY 240) centred at 0806z.
An overall change for the satellite manoeuvre saw the initiation of a large westward drift from 111.8deg E longitude with a Delta V of 7.45 m/s, resulting in a period increase of 626 seconds (including the 303s calculated on the first verified maneuver).
These maneuvers have increased the altitude of the satellite significantly and it is currently drifting at around 2.6 degrees per day.
The neighborhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver. 
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

As of JDAY 240 at 1650z:

JCO providers have verified a maneuver on Fengyun 2F (38049) occurring  on 27 Aug (JDAY 240). The satellite maneuvered from 111.73 deg E longitude with a delta v of 4.06m/s, the effect of which was an increase in westerly drift of 1.3 deg/day, a period of +303s, apogee of +191 km and perigee of +6 km. Neighborhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver. 

A second maneuver has been detected and analysis is on-going.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

As of JDAY 240 at 1330z:

JCO providers have detected a possible maneuver on Fengyun-2F (38049) occurring the 27th of August at approximately 02:56z.
The satellite was located at 111.73 deg E longitude, drifting at -0.04/day. Initial solves of the maneuver show an approximate 300s period change, and an increase in westward drift rate. This out of pattern, large orbit raise has been seen on previous Fengyun satellites as they begin to maneuver to the graveyard belt.

Potential in-plane satellite neighborhood is attached.
Analysis is ongoing.

msgBody.Event_Description:
As of JDAY 241 at 1105z:

JCO providers have verified third maneuver on Fengyun 2F (38049) occurring on 28 Aug 24  (JDAY 241) centred at 0232z.
An overall change for the satellite manoeuvre saw the initiation of a large westward drift from 109.15 deg E longitude with a Delta V of 3.26 m/s, resulting in a period increase of 275.19 seconds.
The maneuver have increased the altitude of the satellite significantly and it is currently drifting at around -3.43 degrees per day.
The neighborhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
As of JDAY 241 at 0115z:

JCO providers have verified two maneuvers on Fengyun 2F (38049) occurring on 27 Aug 24  (JDAY 240) centred at 0806z.
An overall change for the satellite manoeuvre saw the initiation of a large westward drift from 111.8deg E longitude with a Delta V of 3.26 m/s, resulting in a period increase of 275. 19 seconds (including the 303s calculated on the first verified maneuver).
These maneuvers have increased the altitude of the satellite significantly and it is currently drifting at around -3.4 degrees per day.
The neighborhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver. 
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

As of JDAY 240 at 1650z:

JCO providers have verified a maneuver on Fengyun 2F (38049) occurring  on 27 Aug (JDAY 240). The satellite maneuvered from 111.73 deg E longitude with a delta v of 4.06m/s, the effect of which was an increase in westerly drift of 1.3 deg/day, a period of +303s, apogee of +191 km and perigee of +6 km. Neighborhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver. 

A second maneuver has been detected and analysis is on-going.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

As of JDAY 240 at 1330z:

JCO providers have detected a possible maneuver on Fengyun-2F (38049) occurring the 27th of August at approximately 02:56z.
The satellite was located at 111.73 deg E longitude, drifting at -0.04/day. Initial solves of the maneuver show an approximate 300s period change, and an increase in westward drift rate. This out of pattern, large orbit raise has been seen on previous Fengyun satellites as they begin to maneuver to the graveyard belt.

Potential in-plane satellite neighborhood is attached.
Analysis is ongoing.

msgBody.Remarks:
Mission Summary:
The Chinese reusable experimental spacecraft ('Reusable Experimental Spacecraft'; CSSHQ) is the first reusable spacecraft produced by China. It is designed to operate in orbit for some time before returning to the scheduled landing site in China, historically the Lop Nur runway. Reportedly, during the in-orbit operation, the spacecraft will conduct verifications for reusable technologies and space science experiments to provide technical support for the peaceful use of space. This is the third launch and operation of the Chinese reusable space plane.
Source: TRB

msgBody.Event_Description:
As of JDAY 241 at 1910z:

JCO providers have detected a possible maneuver on Fengyun 2F (38049) occurring at ~1407z on 28Aug24 (JDAY 241).
It appears to be increasing its drift and period with this fourth maneuver.
The satellite was located at 107.5deg E longitude.  See attached products. Analysis is ongoing. 

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
As of JDAY 241 at 1105z:

JCO providers have verified third maneuver on Fengyun 2F (38049) occurring on 28 Aug 24  (JDAY 241) centred at 0232z.
An overall change for the satellite manoeuvre saw the initiation of a large westward drift from 109.15 deg E longitude with a Delta V of 3.26 m/s, resulting in a period increase of 275.19 seconds.
The maneuver have increased the altitude of the satellite significantly and it is currently drifting at around -3.43 degrees per day.
The neighborhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
As of JDAY 241 at 0115z:

JCO providers have verified two maneuvers on Fengyun 2F (38049) occurring on 27 Aug 24  (JDAY 240) centred at 0806z.
An overall change for the satellite manoeuvre saw the initiation of a large westward drift from 111.8deg E longitude with a Delta V of 3.26 m/s, resulting in a period increase of 275. 19 seconds (including the 303s calculated on the first verified maneuver).
These maneuvers have increased the altitude of the satellite significantly and it is currently drifting at around -3.4 degrees per day.
The neighborhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver. 
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

As of JDAY 240 at 1650z:

JCO providers have verified a maneuver on Fengyun 2F (38049) occurring  on 27 Aug (JDAY 240). The satellite maneuvered from 111.73 deg E longitude with a delta v of 4.06m/s, the effect of which was an increase in westerly drift of 1.3 deg/day, a period of +303s, apogee of +191 km and perigee of +6 km. Neighborhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver. 

A second maneuver has been detected and analysis is on-going.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

As of JDAY 240 at 1330z:

JCO providers have detected a possible maneuver on Fengyun-2F (38049) occurring the 27th of August at approximately 02:56z.
The satellite was located at 111.73 deg E longitude, drifting at -0.04/day. Initial solves of the maneuver show an approximate 300s period change, and an increase in westward drift rate. This out of pattern, large orbit raise has been seen on previous Fengyun satellites as they begin to maneuver to the graveyard belt.

Potential in-plane satellite neighborhood is attached.
Analysis is ongoing.

Mission Summary:
The Chinese reusable experimental spacecraft ('Reusable Experimental Spacecraft'; CSSHQ) is the first reusable spacecraft produced by China. It is designed to operate in orbit for some time before returning to the scheduled landing site in China, historically the Lop Nur runway. Reportedly, during the in-orbit operation, the spacecraft will conduct verifications for reusable technologies and space science experiments to provide technical support for the peaceful use of space. This is the third launch and operation of the Chinese reusable space plane.

msgBody.Remarks:
Mission Summary:
ChinaSat, also known as Zhongxing, is the brand name of communications satellites operated by China Satellite Communications aka China Satcom, a subsidiary of China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC). As of 28 Aug 2024, at least 20 satellites currently operating in geostationary orbit are owned and operated by China Satcom. These satellites often have multiple names and/or cover names and are broadly categorized into two main categories; Fengho and Shentong. According to the China Space Report, the China Academy of Space Technology (CAST), a related subsidiary of CASC, developed the Fenghuo and Shentong series military communications satellites, positioned in Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) to provide secured digital voice and data communications for military users. Fengho satellites have been described as early warning or tactical communication satellites, whereas Shentong have been described strategic and secured communication satellites.
Source: TRB

Mission Summary:
ChinaSat, also known as Zhongxing, is the brand name of communications satellites operated by China Satellite Communications aka China Satcom, a subsidiary of China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC). As of 28 Aug 2024, at least 20 satellites currently operating in geostationary orbit are owned and operated by China Satcom. These satellites often have multiple names and/or cover names and are broadly categorized into two main categories; Fengho and Shentong. According to the China Space Report, the China Academy of Space Technology (CAST), a related subsidiary of CASC, developed the Fenghuo and Shentong series military communications satellites, positioned in Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) to provide secured digital voice and data communications for military users. Fengho satellites have been described as early warning or tactical communication satellites, whereas Shentong have been described strategic and secured communication satellites.

msgBody.Event_Description:
As of JDAY 242 at 0828z:

JCO providers have indications of successful launch of a Ceres-1S from Yellow Sea  occurring at 0522z.  Based on current information the satellite is likely to be Sun-Synchronous Low Earth Orbit with orbital characteristics of 98.97deg Inclination and 1.11deg RAAN. 
According to PAIR information, payloads carried by the rocket are possibly: Yunyao1 15-17, Jitianxing A-03, Suxing 1-01, Tianfu Gaofen 2. 

Potential in-plane satellite neighborhood updated and attached as a product.  

----------------------------------
As of JDAY 241 at 0522z:

JCO providers have indicated a possible upcoming launch of a Ceres-1S from the Sea Launch Vessel DongFang Hangtiangang, located in the Yellow Sea (36.25N, 123.12E), China. 
The launch is scheduled to occur between 0514z and 0556z on 29 Aug 24 J242 with an expected time of 0522z, carrying an unknown payload. 
Based on current information the satellite is likely to be injected into a Sun-Synchronous Low Earth Orbit with orbital characteristics of 98.97deg Inclination and 1.11deg RAAN. 
Potential co-orbital co-planar satellites list is attached as a product.

msgBody.Remarks:
Mission Summary:
The TJS-1, like the TJS-4 satellite, was built by the Chinese conglomerate CAST.  TJS 1 is a Chinese geostationary satellite reported as a communications technology test satellite, is likely a military Qianshao-3 series SIGINT satellite used for 'wiretapping'. The satellite reported to mainly be used to conduct a test on Ka-band in broadband communication although confirmation that the TJS-1 uses the first big unfurlable mesh (poss 32 m diameter) antenna which is unusual on a Ka-band COMSAT. Also, it doesn't seem likely that an experimental COMSAT would need "8 years of planning and another 6 years of development".  TJS-4, also a military Qianshao-3 series SIGINT satellite, is reported to possibly collect radio transmissions between 250MHz to 1.5GHz (HF/VHF, UHF and L-band), so the TJS-1 may focus on a different frequency range.  The TJS-1 has been positioned at 154.5 East since Sep 2015. 
Source: TAB

msgBody.Event_Description:
JDAY 242 at 1510z:

JCO providers have detected an additional possible maneuver and a photometric change on Fengyun 2F (38049) occurring at 0128z on 29Aug.
The photometric change occurred between the solar phase angles of -130 degrees and -50 degrees. During this change Fengyun 2F (38049) appeared to be up to 3 visual magnitude dimmer.  The purpose of the photometric change is likely related to the maneuver and the graveyarding of the satellite. 
This is expected to be the final in this series of maneuvers.
The satellite was located at 104.3deg E longitude.  
See attached products. Analysis is ongoing.
====================================================================
As of JDAY 241 at 1910z:

JCO providers have detected a possible maneuver on Fengyun 2F (38049) occurring at ~1407z on 28Aug24 (JDAY 241).
It appears to be increasing its drift and period with this fourth maneuver.
The satellite was located at 107.5deg E longitude.  See attached products. Analysis is ongoing. 

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
As of JDAY 241 at 1105z:

JCO providers have verified third maneuver on Fengyun 2F (38049) occurring on 28 Aug 24  (JDAY 241) centred at 0232z.
An overall change for the satellite manoeuvre saw the initiation of a large westward drift from 109.15 deg E longitude with a Delta V of 3.26 m/s, resulting in a period increase of 275.19 seconds.
The maneuver have increased the altitude of the satellite significantly and it is currently drifting at around -3.43 degrees per day.
The neighborhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
As of JDAY 241 at 0115z:

JCO providers have verified two maneuvers on Fengyun 2F (38049) occurring on 27 Aug 24  (JDAY 240) centred at 0806z.
An overall change for the satellite manoeuvre saw the initiation of a large westward drift from 111.8deg E longitude with a Delta V of 3.26 m/s, resulting in a period increase of 275. 19 seconds (including the 303s calculated on the first verified maneuver).
These maneuvers have increased the altitude of the satellite significantly and it is currently drifting at around -3.4 degrees per day.
The neighborhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver. 
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

As of JDAY 240 at 1650z:

JCO providers have verified a maneuver on Fengyun 2F (38049) occurring  on 27 Aug (JDAY 240). The satellite maneuvered from 111.73 deg E longitude with a delta v of 4.06m/s, the effect of which was an increase in westerly drift of 1.3 deg/day, a period of +303s, apogee of +191 km and perigee of +6 km. Neighborhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver. 

A second maneuver has been detected and analysis is on-going.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

As of JDAY 240 at 1330z:

JCO providers have detected a possible maneuver on Fengyun-2F (38049) occurring the 27th of August at approximately 02:56z.
The satellite was located at 111.73 deg E longitude, drifting at -0.04/day. Initial solves of the maneuver show an approximate 300s period change, and an increase in westward drift rate. This out of pattern, large orbit raise has been seen on previous Fengyun satellites as they begin to maneuver to the graveyard belt.

Potential in-plane satellite neighborhood is attached.
Analysis is ongoing.

msgBody.Remarks:
Mission Summary:
ChinaSat, also known as Zhongxing, is the brand name of communications satellites operated by China Satellite Communications aka China Satcom, a subsidiary of China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC). As of 28 Aug 2024, at least 20 satellites currently operating in geostationary orbit are owned and operated by China Satcom. These satellites often have multiple names and/or cover names and are broadly categorized into two main categories; Fengho and Shentong. According to the China Space Report, the China Academy of Space Technology (CAST), a related subsidiary of CASC, developed the Fenghuo and Shentong series military communications satellites, positioned in Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) to provide secured digital voice and data communications for military users. Fengho satellites have been described as early warning or tactical communication satellites, whereas Shentong have been described strategic and secured communication satellites.
Source: TRB

msgBody.Event_Description:
JDAY 242 at 2052z:

JCO providers have verified a maneuver on Fengyun 2F (38049), occurring 29Aug at 0128z.
The satellite maneuvered from 103.28 deg E longitude with a delta v of 9.23 m/s, the effect of which was an 5 sec increase in period to 1452.53 mins.  This may be the final maneuver for Fengyun 2F as it enters the graveyard orbit.

===============================================================
JDAY 242 at 1510z:

JCO providers have detected an additional possible maneuver and a photometric change on Fengyun 2F (38049) occurring at 0128z on 29Aug.
The photometric change occurred between the solar phase angles of -130 degrees and -50 degrees. During this change Fengyun 2F (38049) appeared to be up to 3 visual magnitude dimmer.  The purpose of the photometric change is likely related to the maneuver and the graveyarding of the satellite. 
This is expected to be the final in this series of maneuvers.
The satellite was located at 104.3deg E longitude.  
See attached products. Analysis is ongoing.
====================================================================
As of JDAY 241 at 1910z:

JCO providers have detected a possible maneuver on Fengyun 2F (38049) occurring at ~1407z on 28Aug24 (JDAY 241).
It appears to be increasing its drift and period with this fourth maneuver.
The satellite was located at 107.5deg E longitude.  See attached products. Analysis is ongoing. 

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
As of JDAY 241 at 1105z:

JCO providers have verified third maneuver on Fengyun 2F (38049) occurring on 28 Aug 24  (JDAY 241) centred at 0232z.
An overall change for the satellite manoeuvre saw the initiation of a large westward drift from 109.15 deg E longitude with a Delta V of 3.26 m/s, resulting in a period increase of 275.19 seconds.
The maneuver have increased the altitude of the satellite significantly and it is currently drifting at around -3.43 degrees per day.
The neighborhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
As of JDAY 241 at 0115z:

JCO providers have verified two maneuvers on Fengyun 2F (38049) occurring on 27 Aug 24  (JDAY 240) centred at 0806z.
An overall change for the satellite manoeuvre saw the initiation of a large westward drift from 111.8deg E longitude with a Delta V of 3.26 m/s, resulting in a period increase of 275. 19 seconds (including the 303s calculated on the first verified maneuver).
These maneuvers have increased the altitude of the satellite significantly and it is currently drifting at around -3.4 degrees per day.
The neighborhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver. 
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

As of JDAY 240 at 1650z:

JCO providers have verified a maneuver on Fengyun 2F (38049) occurring  on 27 Aug (JDAY 240). The satellite maneuvered from 111.73 deg E longitude with a delta v of 4.06m/s, the effect of which was an increase in westerly drift of 1.3 deg/day, a period of +303s, apogee of +191 km and perigee of +6 km. Neighborhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver. 

A second maneuver has been detected and analysis is on-going.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

As of JDAY 240 at 1330z:

JCO providers have detected a possible maneuver on Fengyun-2F (38049) occurring the 27th of August at approximately 02:56z.
The satellite was located at 111.73 deg E longitude, drifting at -0.04/day. Initial solves of the maneuver show an approximate 300s period change, and an increase in westward drift rate. This out of pattern, large orbit raise has been seen on previous Fengyun satellites as they begin to maneuver to the graveyard belt.

Potential in-plane satellite neighborhood is attached.
Analysis is ongoing.

Mission Summary:
The Tongxin Jishu Shiyan Weixing-3 (TJS-3) is officially described by China as a communications engineering test satellite. However, lack of public information has lead to the suspicions that this satellite has a military mission. It has been speculated that the satellite might be in fact a military SIGINT or early warning satellite. Approximately a week after launch, an object separated from TJS-3 and is considered a subsatellite (TJS-3 SUBSAT, 43917).
Source: TRB

Mission Summary:
The Chinese reusable experimental spacecraft ('Reusable Experimental Spacecraft'; CSSHQ) is the first reusable spacecraft produced by China. It is designed to operate in orbit for some time before returning to the scheduled landing site in China, historically the Lop Nur runway. Reportedly, during the in-orbit operation, the spacecraft will conduct verifications for reusable technologies and space science experiments to provide technical support for the peaceful use of space. This is the third launch and operation of the Chinese reusable space plane.

JDay 246 at 0035z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a second maneuver on PRC Test Spacecraft 3 (58573) occurring between 1035z and 1107z on 30 Aug 24. PRC Test Spacecraft 3 (58573) is believed to be the third flight of the CSSHQ, a Chinese military reusable test/prototype spacecraft.
The satellite maneuvered with a delta v of 2.86m/s, the effect of which was an increase in period by 2s, bringing its final period to 91.4 mins. 

58573 is still in a re-entry phase that lasts weeks.  For the second spaceplane the de-orbit took place 32 days after the tracking vessel left Durban and 17 days after it turned south after approaching Brazil. The current vessel turned south on 27 Aug and 17 days would lead to 13 September. The current vessel is expected in Cape Town on 20 September with a rough estimate of 8 days transit to reach Cape Town from the expected de-orbit tracking site which would lead to a 12 September date.
Analysis is still on-going.

The specifics of the maneuver are:
--Time of Maneuver: 1035z and 1107z on 30 Aug 24
--Delta V: 2.86 m/s
--Period Change: +2.0031 s
--Apogee Change: +3.73km
--Perigee Change: +8.51km
--Inclination Change: -0.003deg

SUMMARY: JDay 246 at 0035z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a second maneuver on PRC Test Spacecraft 3 (58573) occurring between 1035z and 1107z on 30 Aug 24. PRC Test Spacecraft 3 (58573) is believed to be the third flight of the CSSHQ, a Chinese military reusable test/prototype spacecraft.
The satellite maneuvered with a delta v of 2.86m/s, the effect of which was an increase in period by 2s, bringing its final period to 91.4 mins. 

58573 is still in a re-entry phase that lasts weeks.  For the second spaceplane the de-orbit took place 32 days after the tracking vessel left Durban and 17 days after it turned south after approaching Brazil. The current vessel turned south on 27 Aug and 17 days would lead to 13 September. The current vessel is expected in Cape Town on 20 September with a rough estimate of 8 days transit to reach Cape Town from the expected de-orbit tracking site which would lead to a 12 September date.
Analysis is still on-going.

The communications technology test satellite number 10, or TJS-10 is a Chinese geostationary satellite likely with a technological mission, but may be equipped with a military support payload. JD247 at 0946z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have detected a possible photometric change on TJS-10 (48204), a Chinese military communication and technology satellite. 
This change occurred between the solar phase angles of 70 degrees and 82 degrees. During this change TJS-10 appeared to be 1.5 visual magnitude brighter than usually expected. This photometric change occurred while being in RPO with TJS-3 (43874), a Chinese communication and early warning satellite which performed a photometric change at the same time. But while TJS-3 photometric change matches its usual pattern of life, TJS-10's is out of pattern.

The purpose of this latest photometric change could be maneuvering in order to perform a close approach with TJS-3 with which it has been in RPO for months.

The photometric change reverted back to normal on JDAY246.

TJS-10 is in GEO at 173 east longitude.
Potential in-plane satellite neighborhood is attached.
Analysis is ongoing.

Mission Summary:
Shijian-20 (SJ-20) is a Chinese experimental GEO satellite based on the new DFH-5 Bus equipped with more than a dozen internationally leading technology verification payloads. It also has the mission of new technology verification, and has carried out orbit experiments for a series of key technologies. One source says it has a robotic arm and on board cameras to monitor the operation of the solar panels, the arm and the antennas. SJ-20 is the largest Chinese communications satellite, built with a launch mass of 8 tons.
Source: TAB

There is speculation as to the military purpose of the Gaofen-13 which China reports as 'wild' speculation. Possible Chinese military applications include identifying and tracking U.S. Strike Carrier Group activities, particularly in the SCS. The Gaofen-13 is suspected to be an improved version of the Gaofen-4 satellite with significantly larger optical systems.

JDay 247 at 1457z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a maneuver on Gaofen 13 (46610), a Chinese civilian earth observation satellite, occurring 01Sep2317z.
The satellite maneuvered from 117.97 deg E longitude with a delta v of 9.58 m/s, the effect of which was inclination maintenance and this maneuver decreased the inclination to 0 degs.  Will note that usually these satellites do a bigger inclination change with the RAAN flip, but this satellite has been performing a step-down approach to decrease its inclination with a total of 5 maneuvers starting back on 15Jul2024.  Plot showing this step-down attached for review.  Neighborhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver.

--Time of Maneuver: 01Sep2024 at 2317z

--Apogee Change: +17.97 km

Mission Summary:
Shijian-20 (SJ-20) is a Chinese experimental GEO satellite based on the new DFH-5 Bus equipped with more than a dozen internationally leading technology verification payloads. It also has the mission of new technology verification, and has carried out orbit experiments for a series of key technologies. One source says it has a robotic arm and on board cameras to monitor the operation of the solar panels, the arm and the antennas. SJ-20 is the largest Chinese communications satellite, built with a launch mass of 8 tons.

JDay 248 at 1405z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a maneuver on SY 24C 01 (58650), a Chinese technology test satellite, occurring at 0520z.  This satellite is currently in an RPO with SJ 6-05A (44961), a Chinese science/signals intelligence satellite.  The effect of the maneuver is a decrease of relative distance leading to both objects closing in on another.
The satellite maneuvered from an apogee of 579.44km and a perigee of 579.04km with a delta v of 0.33m/s, the effect of which was an apogee change of 0.725km increasing orbital period by 0.284s. Attached TRIC plot will show the new relative motion.

The specifics of the maneuver are:
--Time of Maneuver: 0520z at 04 Sep 2024, JDay 248

--Perigee Change: -0.269km

msgBody.Email_Subject: NOTSO - Deorbit / 58573 / PRC Test Spacecraft 3 / NE - 216c_06Sep-1553Z - TACREP Notification
msgBody.Follow_Up_Assessment:
JDay 241 1957z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a maneuver on PRC Test Spacecraft 3 (58573), the third flight of the CSSHQ, a Chinese military reusable test/prototype spacecraft, 
 occurring on 27Aug at 2132z.
The satellite boosted its period by 1.67 s bringing its final period to 91.37 mins.  58573 is still in a re-entry phase that lasts weeks.  Analysis is still on-going.

The specifics of the maneuver are:
--Time of Maneuver: 27Aug at 2132z
--Delta V: 2.41 m/s
--Period Change: +1.67 s
--Apogee Change: +1.44 km
--Perigee Change: +1.3 km
--Inclination Change: -0.01 degs

Post Maneuver TLE provided by KBR:  
1 58573U KBR_SV   24241.15398289 +.00154819 +00000-0 +96970-3 0  0001
2 58573  49.9817  91.3728 0002038 301.7313  27.8638 15.7603706000000


================================================================
JDAY 241 at 1450z:

SWF: Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, a possible maneuver has been observed on  PRC Test Spacecraft 3 (58573). 58573 is presumed to be the third flight of the CSSHQ, a Chinese military reusable test/prototype spacecraft. This maneuver could be indications of a possible reentry of the object. 

Pre-maneuver TLE as of 27Aug 2002z provided by KBR:
1 58573U KBR_SV   24240.83507822 -.00142773 +00000-0 -87550-3 0  0002
2 58573  49.9890  93.0689 0001936  15.7794 302.8568 15.7651785600001

1 58573U KBR_SV   24241.15398289 +.00177564 +00000-0 +10010-2 0  0001
2 58573  49.9845  91.3688 0007748 143.2019 186.4123 15.7835817500000
msgBody.Remarks:
Mission Summary:
The Chinese reusable experimental spacecraft ('Reusable Experimental Spacecraft'; CSSHQ) is the first reusable spacecraft produced by China. It is designed to operate in orbit for some time before returning to the scheduled landing site in China, historically the Lop Nur runway. Reportedly, during the in-orbit operation, the spacecraft will conduct verifications for reusable technologies and space science experiments to provide technical support for the peaceful use of space. This is the third launch and operation of the Chinese reusable space plane.
Source: TRB

Mission Summary:
Shijian-20 (SJ-20) is a Chinese experimental GEO satellite based on the new DFH-5 Bus equipped with more than a dozen internationally leading technology verification payloads. It also has the mission of new technology verification, and has carried out orbit experiments for a series of key technologies. One source says it has a robotic arm and on board cameras to monitor the operation of the solar panels, the arm and the antennas. SJ-20 is the largest Chinese communications satellite, built with a launch mass of 8 tons.
Source: TAB

Shijian-20 (SJ-20) is a Chinese experimental GEO satellite based on the new DFH-5 Bus equipped with more than a dozen internationally leading technology verification payloads. It also has the mission of new technology verification, and has carried out orbit experiments for a series of key technologies. msgBody.Event_Description:
JDay 254 1414z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a maneuver and the start of a second maneuver on SY-12 01 (50321), a Chinese military satellite that officially the mission of the satellite is for "space environment exploration and related technology tests" however, it is suspected that it is actually a military test satellite, occurring 10 Sep at 0232z.

The satellite maneuvered from 175.97 deg E longitude with a delta v of 1.31 m/s, the effect of which was a decrease in eastward drift rate from 0.59 E deg/day to 0.14 E deg/day. The maneuver occurred near NSS-11 (26554), a US commercial communications satellite. The maneuver placed SY-12 01 to within 31 km of NSS-11 and into a RPO for 1 rev with the second maneuver appearing to exit the RPO.  This is out of pattern of life for this object in that they usually do an RPO around a Chinese satellite when they turn around, rather than a US satellite.  This maneuver is the start of the SY-12 01 turnaround sequence that it performs as it approaches 180 deg E longitude.  Neighborhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver.

The specifics of the maneuver are:
--Time of Maneuver: 10 Sep at 0232z
--Delta V: 1.31 m/s
--Period Change: +110.11 s
--Apogee Change: +71.79km
--Perigee Change: +0.08 km
--Inclination Change: +0.00

msgBody.Email_Subject: NOTSO - Possible Maneuver / 41838 / SJ-17 / GEO - a605_10Sep-1550Z - TACREP Notification
msgBody.Remarks:
Mission Summary:
China claims the SJ-17 is an experimental satellite used to run communication and broadcast services as well as observe space debris. On 21 Apr 2021, Gen Dickinson (Commander of USSPACECOM) confirmed that the 'SJ-17 is Chinese satellite with a robotic arm' and that Space-based robotic arm technology 'could be used in a future system to grab other satellites.' It is believed to be used for on-orbit space situational awareness (SSA) and close-up inspections. Its activities are consistent with the demonstration of RPO technologies for the purpose of satellite servicing and inspection. 
Source: TAB

***********************************

41838 | SHI JIAN 17 | GEO-GSO / Geostationary | China Satcom (China) | Active - Inclined (aged) / Manoeuverable | Civil/Other | Technology / Technology Test/Prototype | 03/11/2016 (7.86 years old) | 15.0 years | Communications technology demonstration satellite. | SJ-17 is a new technology demonstration geostationary satellite developed by CAST. Once reaching the final orbit, China SatCom will take over and use it for providing communication and broadcasting services, as well as performing technology demonstration including new thruster propulsion test using the "green propellant" ammonium dinitramide (ADN), autonomous navigation, advanced solar cells - and observation of orbital debris and also carries a robotic arm.. | Yes - On-board Propulsion | Propulsion Unknown | Source: Seradata

msgBody.Remarks:
Mission Summary:
Shijian-20 (SJ-20) is a Chinese experimental GEO satellite based on the new DFH-5 Bus equipped with more than a dozen internationally leading technology verification payloads. It also has the mission of new technology verification, and has carried out orbit experiments for a series of key technologies. One source says it has a robotic arm and on board cameras to monitor the operation of the solar panels, the arm and the antennas. SJ-20 is the largest Chinese communications satellite, built with a launch mass of 8 tons.
Source: TAB

msgBody.Remarks:
Mission Summary:
ChinaSat, also known as Zhongxing, is the brand name of communications satellites operated by China Satellite Communications aka China Satcom, a subsidiary of China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC). As of 28 Aug 2024, at least 20 satellites currently operating in geostationary orbit are owned and operated by China Satcom. These satellites often have multiple names and/or cover names and are broadly categorized into two main categories; Fengho and Shentong. According to the China Space Report, the China Academy of Space Technology (CAST), a related subsidiary of CASC, developed the Fenghuo and Shentong series military communications satellites, positioned in Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) to provide secured digital voice and data communications for military users. Fengho satellites have been described as early warning or tactical communication satellites, whereas Shentong have been described strategic and secured communication satellites.

Per Gunter's Space Page, ChinaSat 4A is also known as the ZX 4A (Shen Tong 3A ?), the first of a new series of chinese military satellites. The first of these satellites was launched in August 2024 and was given the designation ZX 4A (ChinaSat 4A).
https://space.skyrocket.de/doc_sdat/zx-4a.htm
Source: TRB

msgBody.Remarks:
Mission Summary:
China claims the SJ-17 is an experimental satellite used to run communication and broadcast services as well as observe space debris. On 21 Apr 2021, Gen Dickinson (Commander of USSPACECOM) confirmed that the 'SJ-17 is Chinese satellite with a robotic arm' and that Space-based robotic arm technology 'could be used in a future system to grab other satellites.' It is believed to be used for on-orbit space situational awareness (SSA) and close-up inspections. Its activities are consistent with the demonstration of RPO technologies for the purpose of satellite servicing and inspection. 
Source: TAB

msgBody.Remarks:
Mission Summary:
The TJS-1, like the TJS-4 satellite, was built by the Chinese conglomerate CAST.  TJS 1 is a Chinese geostationary satellite reported as a communications technology test satellite, is likely a military Qianshao-3 series SIGINT satellite used for 'wiretapping'. The satellite reported to mainly be used to conduct a test on Ka-band in broadband communication although confirmation that the TJS-1 uses the first big unfurlable mesh (poss 32 m diameter) antenna which is unusual on a Ka-band COMSAT. Also, it doesn't seem likely that an experimental COMSAT would need "8 years of planning and another 6 years of development".  TJS-4, also a military Qianshao-3 series SIGINT satellite, is reported to possibly collect radio transmissions between 250MHz to 1.5GHz (HF/VHF, UHF and L-band), so the TJS-1 may focus on a different frequency range.  The TJS-1 has been positioned at 154.5 East since Sep 2015. 
Source: TRB

msgBody.Remarks:
Mission Summary:
Shijian-20 (SJ-20) is a Chinese experimental GEO satellite based on the new DFH-5 Bus equipped with more than a dozen internationally leading technology verification payloads. It also has the mission of new technology verification, and has carried out orbit experiments for a series of key technologies. One source says it has a robotic arm and on board cameras to monitor the operation of the solar panels, the arm and the antennas. SJ-20 is the largest Chinese communications satellite, built with a launch mass of 8 tons.
Source: TAB

Mission Summary:
ChinaSat, also known as Zhongxing, is the brand name of communications satellites operated by China Satellite Communications aka China Satcom, a subsidiary of China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC). As of 28 Aug 2024, at least 20 satellites currently operating in geostationary orbit are owned and operated by China Satcom. These satellites often have multiple names and/or cover names and are broadly categorized into two main categories; Fengho and Shentong. According to the China Space Report, the China Academy of Space Technology (CAST), a related subsidiary of CASC, developed the Fenghuo and Shentong series military communications satellites, positioned in Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) to provide secured digital voice and data communications for military users. Fengho satellites have been described as early warning or tactical communication satellites, whereas Shentong have been described strategic and secured communication satellites.

Per Gunter's Space Page, ChinaSat 4A is also known as the ZX 4A (Shen Tong 3A ?), the first of a new series of chinese military satellites. The first of these satellites was launched in August 2024 and was given the designation ZX 4A (ChinaSat 4A).
https://space.skyrocket.de/doc_sdat/zx-4a.htm

SUMMARY: JDay 255 0220z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a manoevure of Chinasat 4A (60606), an active / maneuverable Chinese military communications satellite, occurring at 0145-0200z 10 Sep 24 (JDay 254).

Chinasat 4A maneuvered from 118deg E longitude with a delta v of 0.15m/s, the effect of which was a period change of 7.5s and a small adjustment in easterly GEO drift rate. A manoeuvre of this size is in line with a station keeping manoeuvre.

See attached products for neighbourhood analysis.

Mission Summary:
ChinaSat, also known as Zhongxing, is the brand name of communications satellites operated by China Satellite Communications aka China Satcom, a subsidiary of China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC). As of 28 Aug 2024, at least 20 satellites currently operating in geostationary orbit are owned and operated by China Satcom. These satellites often have multiple names and/or cover names and are broadly categorized into two main categories; Fengho and Shentong. According to the China Space Report, the China Academy of Space Technology (CAST), a related subsidiary of CASC, developed the Fenghuo and Shentong series military communications satellites, positioned in Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) to provide secured digital voice and data communications for military users. Fengho satellites have been described as early warning or tactical communication satellites, whereas Shentong have been described strategic and secured communication satellites.

Per Gunter's Space Page, ChinaSat 4A is also known as the ZX 4A (Shen Tong 3A ?), the first of a new series of chinese military satellites. The first of these satellites was launched in August 2024 and was given the designation ZX 4A (ChinaSat 4A).
https://space.skyrocket.de/doc_sdat/zx-4a.htm

msgBody.Event_Description:
J255 0330z

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have indications of the size of the second manoeuvre performed by SY-12 01 (50321) in its sequence to reverse GEO drift. SY-12 01 maneuvered from around 176deg E at ~1430z 10 Sep with a delta v of approximately 2m/s, resulting in a period change of approximately 175s. In sequence with the already reported verified manoeuvre at 0232z 10Sep, SY-12 01 is now drifting west at approximately 0.55deg/day, reversing its prior drift rate. SY-12 01 is a Chinese military satellite with an official mission of "space environment exploration and related technology tests", however it is suspected to be a military test satellite.
During its drift reversal sequence, SY-12 01 came to within ~53 km of NSS-11 (26554) - a US commercial communications satellite - as previously reported. See attached relative distance charts and TRICs showing SY-12 01 approaching NSS-11, performing brief encompassing proximity operations, and maneuvering to reverse drift and start moving away. The Geostationary Shiyan satellites have historically reversed drift around 17.5degE and 178degE, meaning this sequence is within pattern of life. The reversal sequences have also resulted in RPOs, but usually around Chinese satellites:

- 50321 around 49011 TIANLIAN 1-O5 in August of 2022
- 50322 around 47613 TJS-6 in November 2022

Other reversal sequences have also resulted in close approaches with other satellites.

JCO will continue to monitor to verify this manoeuvre.

JDay 254 1414z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a maneuver and the following of a second maneuver on SY-12 01 (50321), occurring on 10 Sep at 0232z. It is a Chinese military satellite with an official mission of "space environment exploration and related technology tests" however, it is suspected to be a military test satellite.

The satellite maneuvered from 175.97 deg E longitude with a delta v of 1.31 m/s, the effect of which was a decrease in eastward drift rate from 0.59 E deg/day to 0.14 E deg/day. The maneuver occurred near NSS-11 (26554), a US commercial communications satellite and placed SY-12 01 within 31 km of NSS-11. It is currently in an RPO with NSS-11 for 1 rev following with the second maneuver which appearing to be exiting the RPO.  This is not within its PoL as SY-12 01 usually performs RPO with another Chinese satellite when performing a turnaround maneuver, rather than against a US satellite.  This maneuver is the start of the SY-12 01 turnaround sequence as it approaches 180 deg E longitude.  Neighbourhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver.

The specifics of the maneuver are:
--Time of Maneuver: 10 Sep at 0232z
--Delta V: 1.31 m/s
--Period Change: +110.11 s
--Apogee Change: +71.79km
--Perigee Change: +0.08 km
--Inclination Change: +0.00
--Current Drift Rate: 0.14 E deg/day

JDAY 255 0953z

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have detected a possible Photometric change on 43874, TJS-3, Chinese dual communications satellite. JDay 255 at 1555z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a maneuver on SY-12 01 (50321), occurring at 1430z on 10 Sep (JDAY 254).  It is a Chinese military satellite with an official mission of "space environment exploration and related technology tests" however, it is suspected to be a military test satellite.

The satellite is no longer is RPO conditions with NSS-11 (26554).

The satellite maneuvered from around 176 deg E at 1430z 10 Sep with a delta v of approximately 2m/s, the effect of which was the initiation of a westward drift, and a period change of approximately 170s.

The specifics of the maneuver are:
--Time of Maneuver: 1430z
--Delta V: 2.02 m/s
--Period Change: +170s
--Apogee Change: +14.10 km
--Perigee Change: +96.75 km
--Inclination Change: 0.002 deg
--Current Drift Rate: 0.71 deg/day W

Post Maneuver Current TLE as of 1445z provided by EXO:

1 50321U 21129A   24255.59365539 +.00000000 +00000-0 +00000-0 0  0013
2 50321   2.0009  89.4178 0001720 310.9441 339.8576  1.00111929 00019

=================================================================

J255 0330z

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have indications of the size of the second manoeuvre performed by SY-12 01 (50321) in its sequence to reverse GEO drift. SY-12 01 maneuvered from around 176deg E at ~1430z 10 Sep with a delta v of approximately 2m/s, resulting in a period change of approximately 175s. In sequence with the already reported verified manoeuvre at 0232z 10Sep, SY-12 01 is now drifting west at approximately 0.55deg/day, reversing its prior drift rate. SY-12 01 is a Chinese military satellite with an official mission of "space environment exploration and related technology tests", however it is suspected to be a military test satellite.
During its drift reversal sequence, SY-12 01 came to within ~53 km of NSS-11 (26554) - a US commercial communications satellite - as previously reported. See attached relative distance charts and TRICs showing SY-12 01 approaching NSS-11, performing brief encompassing proximity operations, and maneuvering to reverse drift and start moving away. The Geostationary Shiyan satellites have historically reversed drift around 17.5degE and 178degE, meaning this sequence is within pattern of life. The reversal sequences have also resulted in RPOs, but usually around Chinese satellites:

- 50321 around 49011 TIANLIAN 1-O5 in August of 2022
- 50322 around 47613 TJS-6 in November 2022

Other reversal sequences have also resulted in close approaches with other satellites.

JCO will continue to monitor to verify this manoeuvre.

JDay 254 1414z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a maneuver and the following of a second maneuver on SY-12 01 (50321), occurring on 10 Sep at 0232z. It is a Chinese military satellite with an official mission of "space environment exploration and related technology tests" however, it is suspected to be a military test satellite.

The satellite maneuvered from 175.97 deg E longitude with a delta v of 1.31 m/s, the effect of which was a decrease in eastward drift rate from 0.59 E deg/day to 0.14 E deg/day. The maneuver occurred near NSS-11 (26554), a US commercial communications satellite and placed SY-12 01 within 31 km of NSS-11. It is currently in an RPO with NSS-11 for 1 rev following with the second maneuver which appearing to be exiting the RPO.  This is not within its PoL as SY-12 01 usually performs RPO with another Chinese satellite when performing a turnaround maneuver, rather than against a US satellite.  This maneuver is the start of the SY-12 01 turnaround sequence as it approaches 180 deg E longitude.  Neighbourhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver.

The specifics of the maneuver are:
--Time of Maneuver: 10 Sep at 0232z

--Period Change: +110.11 s

--Perigee Change: +0.08 km

msgBody.Remarks:
Mission Summary:
China claims the SJ-17 is an experimental satellite used to run communication and broadcast services as well as observe space debris. On 21 Apr 2021, Gen Dickinson (Commander of USSPACECOM) confirmed that the 'SJ-17 is Chinese satellite with a robotic arm' and that Space-based robotic arm technology 'could be used in a future system to grab other satellites.' It is believed to be used for on-orbit space situational awareness (SSA) and close-up inspections. Its activities are consistent with the demonstration of RPO technologies for the purpose of satellite servicing and inspection. 
Source: TAB

***********************************

Mission Summary:
ChinaSat, also known as Zhongxing, is the brand name of communications satellites operated by China Satellite Communications aka China Satcom, a subsidiary of China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC). As of 28 Aug 2024, at least 20 satellites currently operating in geostationary orbit are owned and operated by China Satcom. These satellites often have multiple names and/or cover names and are broadly categorized into two main categories; Fengho and Shentong. According to the China Space Report, the China Academy of Space Technology (CAST), a related subsidiary of CASC, developed the Fenghuo and Shentong series military communications satellites, positioned in Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) to provide secured digital voice and data communications for military users. Fengho satellites have been described as early warning or tactical communication satellites, whereas Shentong have been described strategic and secured communication satellites.

Per Gunter's Space Page, ChinaSat 4A is also known as the ZX 4A (Shen Tong 3A ?), the first of a new series of chinese military satellites. The first of these satellites was launched in August 2024 and was given the designation ZX 4A (ChinaSat 4A).
Source: https://space.skyrocket.de/doc_sdat/zx-4a.htm

JDay 260 at 1104z:

Based on available PAIR data, JCO providers have indicated a possible upcoming launch of a Angara 1.2 from Plesetsk, Russia occurring between 17 to 30 Sep with a launch window of 0700 to 0900z daily, possibly carrying a Strela-3M/Rodni, military communication satellite, EO MKA, military unknown mission and a Razbeg, military optical satellite. msgBody.Remarks:
58204 | TJS-10 | GEO-GSO / Geostationary | CASC - China Aerospace Science and Technology Corp (China) | Active / Manoeuverable | Military | Communications / Communications - Experimental,Technology / Technology Test/Prototype | 03/11/2023 (0.87 years old) | 15.0 years | Tongxin Jishu Shiyan Weixing-10 or Communications Engineering Test Satellite-10. Possible military mission. | Yes - On-board Propulsion | Propulsion Unknown | Source: Seradata

The communications technology test satellite number 10, or TJS-10 is a Chinese geostationary satellite likely with a technological mission, but may be equipped with a military support payload. The purpose may be tests of multi-band, high-speed satellite communication technology. Some variants of the TJS are suspected of having a SIGINT payload, while others are suspected of having an early warning capability (similar to the US SBIRS).

<SatelliteDossier>

43874 | TJS-3 MAIN | GEO-GSO / Geostationary | Chinese Ministry of Defence (China) | Active / Manoeuverable | Military | Communications / Communications - Data Relay,Early Warning / Early Warning,Signals Intelligence / Signals Intelligence - Electronic | 24/12/2018 (5.73 years old) | 15.0 years | Communications Engineering Test Satellite but may have secondary missile defence/early warning/space ELINT role. | TJS-3 believed be an experimental communications or data relay or Sigint satellite. It has a large unfurlable antenna like TJS-1. There are also reports that the satellite may be an Early Warning satellite for China's Ballistic Missile Defence Organisation that will work in a similar fashion the US Space Based Infra-Red Sensor (SBIRS) system. Carries multi-bands and high-rate satellite communication. | Yes - On-board Propulsion | Propulsion Unknown | Gateway Down: S | User Down: Ka,X | ,TJS-3 SUBSAT | Source: Seradata

msgBody.Event_Description:
JDay 260 1555z

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have detected a possible Photometric change on TJS-10 (58204), Chinese, military communications experimental satellite.  This change was detected by only one sensor, so cannot say if this is 100% accurate or not.

The change occurred between the solar phase angles of -100 degrees and -90 degrees. During this change TJS-10 appeared to be ~1.4 visual magnitude brighter.  The purpose of the photometric change is unknown. However, at the time of the change, it had a close approach of ~49km with TJS-3 (43874) on 16Sep at 0602z, with TJS-10 having good lighting. The satellite is in GEO at 172.9 E longitude and is geo-synchronous. 

Will note that TJS-10 and TJS-3 have been in an RPO with each other for an extended time period. Potential in-plane satellite neighborhood is attached.  Analysis is ongoing.

The communications technology test satellite number 10, or TJS-10 is a Chinese geostationary satellite likely with a technological mission, but may be equipped with a military support payload. The purpose may be tests of multi-band, high-speed satellite communication technology. Some variants of the TJS are suspected of having a SIGINT payload, while others are suspected of having an early warning capability (similar to the US SBIRS).

JDAY 261 1357z

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers detected a possible Photometric change on TJS-10 (58204), Chinese, military communications experimental satellite on JDAY 260. The change occurred between the solar phase angles of -100 degrees and -90 degrees. At the time this change was detected by only one sensor, and the change could not be verified. Today on JDAY 261, TJS-10 (58204) appeared to return to its nominal signature. 

JDay 260 1555z

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have detected a possible Photometric change on TJS-10 (58204), Chinese, military communications experimental satellite.  This change was detected by only one sensor, so cannot say if this is 100% accurate or not.

The change occurred between the solar phase angles of -100 degrees and -90 degrees. During this change TJS-10 appeared to be ~1.4 visual magnitude brighter.  The purpose of the photometric change is unknown. However, at the time of the change, it had a close approach of ~49km with TJS-3 (43874) on 16Sep at 0602z, with TJS-10 having good lighting. The satellite is in GEO at 172.9 E longitude and is geo-synchronous. 

Will note that TJS-10 and TJS-3 have been in an RPO with each other for an extended time period. Potential in-plane satellite neighborhood is attached.  Analysis is ongoing.

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have detected a possible Photometric change on TJS-10 (58204), Chinese, military communications experimental satellite.  This change was detected by only one sensor, so cannot say if this is 100% accurate or not.

msgBody.Remarks:
Luch 5X (OLYMP K-2) is a Russian geostationary satellite built for the Russian Ministry of Defense and the Russian intelligence agency, FSB. While the purpose of the satellites has not been officially disclosed, the satellites are believed to serve two purposes. The first purpose is to conduct signals intelligence (SIGINT) and the second is to provide secure communications lines for governmental use. The Luch designation, which is also used to refer to the Russian Satellite Data Relay Network (SDRN), hints at the satellites being used in a data relay role.

JDay 262 at 0201z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a second manoeuvre on COSMOS 2558 (53323), Russian military servicing/ inspection satellite, occurring at 1256z on 17 Sep 24 JDAY 261.

The satellite manoeuvred with a delta v of 2.8m/s, the effect of which was a period change of ~3 sec.  Neighbourhood of nearby HRR objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this manoeuvre.

Closest approach will be with KNOWN OBJECT 90106 at a minimum distance of 37km at 0827z 18 Sep 24 JDAY 262.

Mission Summary:
Luch 5X (OLYMP K-2) is a Russian geostationary satellite built for the Russian Ministry of Defense and the Russian intelligence agency, FSB. While the purpose of the satellites has not been officially disclosed, the satellites are believed to serve two purposes. The first purpose is to conduct signals intelligence (SIGINT) and the second is to provide secure communications lines for governmental use. The Luch designation, which is also used to refer to the Russian Satellite Data Relay Network (SDRN), hints at the satellites being used in a data relay role.
