JDay 262 at 1911z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers detected another possible maneuver on Luch Olymp 2 (55841), a Russian military communications satellite with Signal and Electronic Intelligence capabilities, occurring ~18Sep at 0644z.
The satellite was located at 0.9 deg W longitude when it started to decrease its drift rate.  Based off of initial indications it appears it is decreasing its period and is potentially parking east of Intelsat 1002 (28358),  a US commercial communications satellite, and west of Thor 5 (32487), Thor 6 (36033) and Thor 7 (40613), Norwegian commercial communication satellites. Mission Summary:
Cosmos 2558 is a Russia military (14F150 Nivelir) 'inspector satellite' used for orbital surveillance. Cosmos-2519 (42798) and Cosmos 2542 (44797) are predecessor satellite also part of the Nivelir program. Cosmos 2558 will likely to deploy a sub-satellite which in turn may fire what has been described by US intelligence sources as a 'projectile'. It was reported that the orbital plane of USA 326 would pass right over Plestesk at the time of launch of Cosmos 2558, providing an early indication that USA 326 will be its first satellite of interest.

Source: <SatelliteDossier>

BD 3M (Beidou 3M) satellites are the MEO component of the 3rd phase of the chinese Beidou (Compass) satellite navigation system, which, in contrast to GPS and GLONASS, uses both geostationary satellites and satellites in intermediate orbit.

This series provides the satellites for the intermediate constellation called "Compass-M" in 12-hours orbits. Ulitmately, the MEO constellation will comprise 27 satellites.

Source: https://space.skyrocket.de/doc_sdat/bd-3m-2.htm

Mission Summary: Luch 5X (OLYMP K-2) is a Russian geostationary satellite built for the Russian Ministry of Defense and the Russian intelligence agency, FSB. While the purpose of the satellites has not been officially disclosed, the satellites are believed to serve two purposes. The first purpose is to conduct signals intelligence (SIGINT) and the second is to provide secure communications lines for governmental use. The Luch designation, which is also used to refer to the Russian Satellite Data Relay Network (SDRN), hints at the satellites being used in a data relay role.
Source: JB

JDay 244 at 1230z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers detected a possible maneuver on LUCH (OLYMP) 2 (55841), occurring at 0249z on 01SEP25.

The satellite was located at 61.97 degs E longitude. Based off of initial indications it appears this maneuver has resulted in a minor reduction in Westward drift to a final longitudinal drift rate of -0.021 deg/day. The maneuver expended 0.12 m/s Delta-V.

This suggests a continued parking intention with INTELSAT 39 which is the current RPO target as described in the pervious NOTSOs. The maneuver has also resulted in a decrease of RAAN, with a final RAAN of 125.499 deg. The differential correction result attached is derived from Passive Radio Frequency from KRATOS data.

Analysis of this event is ongoing.

LUCH (OLYMP) 2 (55841) is a Russian satellite that supports military operations. The mission of LUCH (OLYMP) 2 is to conduct Electronic Intelligence Operations to spy on communications satellites. It is also suspected of conducting Russian Espionage activities.

Mission Summary:
Shijian-20 (SJ-20) is a Chinese experimental GEO satellite based on the new DFH-5 Bus equipped with more than a dozen internationally leading technology verification payloads. It also has the mission of new technology verification, and has carried out orbit experiments for a series of key technologies. One source says it has a robotic arm and on board cameras to monitor the operation of the solar panels, the arm and the antennas. SJ-20 is the largest Chinese communications satellite, built with a launch mass of 8 tons.
Source: TRB

JDay 246 at 1854z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a maneuver on SJ-20 (44910) occurring at 0545z on 03Sept (JDay 246).

The satellite maneuvered from 83.1 degs E longitude with a delta-v of 0.19 m/s, resulting in a 10 second period increase, increasing westward drift. This maneuver increased both the distance between SJ-20 and KBR UCT 82.0 E (70820) at their POCA and the distance between SJ-20 and CMS-01(47256) at their POCA to >30kms.

This maneuver does not appear to be a station-keeping maneuver and is not within the historical pattern of life for this object. Neighborhood of nearby objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver.

SJ-20 (44910) is a Chinese satellite that supports commercial operations. The mission of SJ-20 is experimental communications and technology testing.

--Time of Maneuver: 03Sep0545z

--Apogee Change: +3.7 km

JDAY 246, 2330z

Mission Summary:
Luch 5X (OLYMP K-2) is a Russian geostationary satellite built for the Russian Ministry of Defense and the Russian intelligence agency, FSB. While the purpose of the satellites has not been officially disclosed, the satellites are believed to serve two purposes. The first purpose is to conduct signals intelligence (SIGINT) and the second is to provide secure communications lines for governmental use. The Luch designation, which is also used to refer to the Russian Satellite Data Relay Network (SDRN), hints at the satellites being used in a data relay role.
Source: TRB

JDay 247 at 0045z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers detected a verified maneuver on LUCH OLYMP 2 (55841), occurring at 1414z on 03SEP / JDAY246.  The maneuver appears to be station keeping and within POL.

LUCH (OLYMP) 2 and INTELSAT 39 (Rank 4) have maintained RPO conditions since March 2025 (see most recently closed thread a7ed, and attached TRIC plot). This maneuver has not increased those conditions. The objects are continuing to separate with 25.5km as the next minimum distance at 1045 UTC on 4 Sep, INTELSAT 39 will have favourable visibility. 

LUCH OLYMP 2 was located at 61.99 degs E longitude.  A small period change of -1.9 seconds with natural perturbation has been observed by providers. 

Click link above to view products. Analysis is ongoing.

LUCH (OLYMP) 2 (55841) is a Russian satellite that supports military operations. The mission of LUCH (OLYMP) 2 is to conduct Electronic Intelligence Operations to spy on communications satellites. It is also suspected of engaging in Russian espionage activities.

INTELSAT 39 (44476) is a USA satellite that supports commercial operations. The mission of INTELSAT 39 (44476) is Communications. Providing high-throughput service including broadband Internet and direct TV to Africa, Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and the Indian Ocean region.

--Time of Maneuver: 03SEP1414z
--Delta V: 0.1282 m/s
--Period Change: 2.80 secs

--Perigee Change: 0.63 km

JDAY 247, 0705z

Mission Summary:
The payload for this launch is speculated to be the Shiyan-29 (SY-29).  The SY-series is part of Chinas long-running Shiyan (Experimental) satellite series, which has been used since 2004 to test a wide range of space technologies, including rendezvous and proximity operations, Earth and space environment monitoring, and satellite servicing. SY-29 is reportedly launching around September 5, 2025, aboard a Chang Zheng-3C (CZ-3C) rocket with a YZ-1 upper stage from Xichang, though no official mission objectives, orbital data, or payload details have been disclosed. Like other Shiyan missions, its purpose is presumed to be experimental or technology-demonstration in nature, but information remains scarce due to the programs high level of secrecy, with most insights coming from independent trackers and spaceflight forums rather than official Chinese sources.
Source: RC

Mission Summary:
The payload for this launch is speculated to be the Shiyan-29 (SY-29).  The SY-series is part of Chinas long-running Shiyan (Experimental) satellite series, which has been used since 2004 to test a wide range of space technologies, including rendezvous and proximity operations, Earth and space environment monitoring, and satellite servicing. SY-29 is reportedly launching around September 5, 2025, aboard a Chang Zheng-3C (CZ-3C) rocket with a YZ-1 upper stage from Xichang, though no official mission objectives, orbital data, or payload details have been disclosed. Like other Shiyan missions, its purpose is presumed to be experimental or technology-demonstration in nature, but information remains scarce due to the programs high level of secrecy, with most insights coming from independent trackers and spaceflight forums rather than official Chinese sources.

msgBody.Remarks:
JDay 251 at 0600z:

PAIR

Mission Summary:
Shijian-20 (SJ-20) is a Chinese experimental GEO satellite based on the new DFH-5 Bus equipped with more than a dozen internationally leading technology verification payloads. It also has the mission of new technology verification, and has carried out orbit experiments for a series of key technologies. One source says it has a robotic arm and on board cameras to monitor the operation of the solar panels, the arm and the antennas. SJ-20 is the largest Chinese communications satellite, built with a launch mass of 8 tons.
Source: JB

JDay 251 at 0417z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have detected a Photometric change on SJ-20 (44910). This change occurred between the solar phase angles of 116deg to -96deg and appeared to be 0.5 visual magnitude brighter.
 
The cause of the change may be associated with a close approach with CHINASAT 1E (53813) at 06SEP1247z at 68.8km and satellite SJ-20 had bad lighting to view CHINASAT 1E. This photometric variation is consistent with the historical pattern of life for this object. Analysis is ongoing.
 
The satellite is in GEO and is currently at 81.5378 degs E longitude and is drifting at 0.5938W deg/day. Neighborhood is provided. Click link above to view products
 
SJ-20 (44910) is a Chinese satellite that supports military operations. The mission of SJ-20 is high throughput communications, and technology testing and prototyping.
 
CHINASAT 1E (53813) is a Chinese satellite that supports commercial operations. The mission of CHINASAT 1E  is military communications satellite albeit with the official function of direct broadcasting satellite.

COSMOS 2513 (41121) is a Russian satellite that supports military operations. The mission of COSMOS 2513 is to provide relay links to low Earth reconnaissance satellites.

JDAY 247, 1028Z

Mission Summary:
The Chinese satellite TJS-12 (NORAD ID: 62374), launched on December 20, 2024, via a Long March 3B rocket from Xichang Satellite Launch Center, is a classified geostationary satellite operated by the People's Liberation Army Strategic Support Force (PLA SSF). Officially described as a communication engineering test satellite for satellite communications, radio, television, and data transmission, its true mission remains opaque, with speculation suggesting it may perform signals intelligence (SIGINT) or missile warning functions, similar to other TJS-series satellites. Positioned in a geostationary orbit over 146.5E with an inclination of 1.8 (initially 2.0), TJS-12 was initially launched into a geostationary transfer orbit (GTO) with a 28.4 inclination and a semi-major axis of 17,991 km, transitioning to its final orbit within 710 days. Built by the Shanghai Academy of Spaceflight Technology, it is part of the secretive Tongxin Jishu Shiyan (TJS) program, which has drawn attention for its potential military applications, including spoofing and satellite inspection capabilities, amid limited public disclosure from Chinese authorities.
Source: RC

msgBody.Event_Description:
JDay 251 at 1200z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have detected a Photometric change on TJS-12, (62374). This change occurred between the solar phase angles of -50 to -46 and appeared to be 1.3 visual magnitude brighter with the change occurring between the period 1045z and 1115z on 8 Sep 25 JDAY151. The two outliers at -50.5 deg and -47.5 deg reaching from 8.1 VisMag to 7 VisMag are disregarded as being tracked by only one sensor.

The previous change which occurred between the solar phase angles of 40 to 130 between 21 Aug and 4 Sept 2025 which appeared to be 2.5 total visual magnitude brighter is now returning to POL of TJS-12 from 12 visual magnitude down to 13 as of 8 Sept 2025.
 
The change could also be due to its recent close approach of 68.7km with SY-9(47851) on 08 SEP 2025 @1135z. Analysis is ongoing.
 
The satellite is in GEO and is currently at 146.5 degs E longitude and is drifting at -0.02 W deg/day. Neighborhood is provided. Click link above to view products
 
TJS-12 (62374) is a Chinese satellite that supports commercial operations. The mission of TJS-12 is to support satellite communications, radio and television, data transmission, and other services, and to carry out relevant technical tests and verification.

Shiyan 9 (47851) is a Chinese Satellite that supports military operations. The mission of SY-9 is earth observation and imaging and was originally thought to be the re-flight of the TJS-6 to provide early warning.

04 Sep, JDAY 247, 0625z

Mission Summary:
The Tongxin Jishu Shiyan-19 (TJS-19) satellite, identified by NORAD ID 63924, is a classified Chinese experimental spacecraft launched on May 12, 2025, at approximately 18:09 UTC from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center (LC3) aboard a Long March 3C/G2 rocket (Y7), marking the vehicle's seventh flight and China's 25th orbital mission of the year; developed by the Shanghai Academy of Spaceflight Technology (SAST) under the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC), TJS-19 was inserted into a geosynchronous transfer orbit (GTO) with an apogee of around 35,800 km, perigee of 200 km, and inclination of 28.5, from which it used onboard propulsion to reach geostationary orbit (GEO) at approximately 36,000 km altitude for operations; officially described as a communication technology experiment satellite primarily for verifying multi-band, high-speed satellite communication technologies, including data transmission, radio, and television services, the mission aligns with the opaque TJS series' pattern of vague disclosures and last-minute airspace closures, leading Western analysts to speculate on underlying military objectives such as signals intelligence (SIGINT), early warning missile detection, or satellite inspection activities to support the People's Liberation Army (PLA), potentially as part of the Qianshao-3 or Huoyan-1 subclasses; with an estimated mass of 1,0002,500 kg on an SAST DFH-4 or similar bus, TJS-19 contributes to China's expanding GEO constellation of 17 active TJS satellites (skipping TJS-8 and TJS-18), enhancing strategic space domain awareness amid growing counterspace demonstrations, and remains operational as of September 2025 with no public images or detailed results released.
Source: RC

JDAY 247, 0705z

Mission Summary:
The payload for this launch is speculated to be the Shiyan-29 (SY-29).  The SY-series is part of Chinas long-running Shiyan (Experimental) satellite series, which has been used since 2004 to test a wide range of space technologies, including rendezvous and proximity operations, Earth and space environment monitoring, and satellite servicing. SY-29 is reportedly launching around September 5, 2025, aboard a Chang Zheng-3C (CZ-3C) rocket with a YZ-1 upper stage from Xichang, though no official mission objectives, orbital data, or payload details have been disclosed. Like other Shiyan missions, its purpose is presumed to be experimental or technology-demonstration in nature, but information remains scarce due to the programs high level of secrecy, with most insights coming from independent trackers and spaceflight forums rather than official Chinese sources.
Source: RC

msgBody.Remarks:
JDAY 251, 1606z

Mission Summary:
The Chamran-1 research satellite, successfully launched on September 14, 2024, by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) using the Qaem-100 solid-fuel rocket, is a 60 kg domestically developed satellite placed into a 550 km low Earth orbit to advance Iran's space technology capabilities. Designed and built by Iran Electronics Industries (SAIran) in collaboration with the Aerospace Research Institute and private firms, its primary mission is to test hardware and software systems for validating orbital maneuvering technology, including altitude and phase adjustments, critical for future satellite constellations. Secondary objectives include evaluating cold gas propulsion subsystems and navigation and attitude control systems, with the satellite successfully transmitting its first signals hours after launch. Of note, Chamran-1 demonstrated the ability to conduct a precise orbital rendezvous, achieving phase alignment within 0.05 and altitude differences of just a few kilometers relative to its launch vehicle,

Mission Summary:
The Chamran-1 research satellite, successfully launched on September 14, 2024, by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) using the Qaem-100 solid-fuel rocket, is a 60 kg domestically developed satellite placed into a 550 km low Earth orbit to advance Iran's space technology capabilities. Designed and built by Iran Electronics Industries (SAIran) in collaboration with the Aerospace Research Institute and private firms, its primary mission is to test hardware and software systems for validating orbital maneuvering technology, including altitude and phase adjustments, critical for future satellite constellations. Secondary objectives include evaluating cold gas propulsion subsystems and navigation and attitude control systems, with the satellite successfully transmitting its first signals hours after launch. Of note, Chamran-1 demonstrated the ability to conduct a precise orbital rendezvous, achieving phase alignment within 0.05 and altitude differences of just a few kilometers relative to its launch vehicle,

Mission Summary:
The payload for this launch is speculated to be the Shiyan-29 (SY-29).  The SY-series is part of Chinas long-running Shiyan (Experimental) satellite series, which has been used since 2004 to test a wide range of space technologies, including rendezvous and proximity operations, Earth and space environment monitoring, and satellite servicing. SY-29 is reportedly launching around September 5, 2025, aboard a Chang Zheng-3C (CZ-3C) rocket with a YZ-1 upper stage from Xichang, though no official mission objectives, orbital data, or payload details have been disclosed. Like other Shiyan missions, its purpose is presumed to be experimental or technology-demonstration in nature, but information remains scarce due to the programs high level of secrecy, with most insights coming from independent trackers and spaceflight forums rather than official Chinese sources.

The payload for this launch is speculated to be the Shiyan-29 (SY-29).  The SY-series is part of Chinas long-running Shiyan (Experimental) satellite series, which has been used since 2004 to test a wide range of space technologies, including rendezvous and proximity operations, Earth and space environment monitoring, and satellite servicing. SY-29 is reportedly launching around September 5, 2025, aboard a Chang Zheng-3C (CZ-3C) rocket with a YZ-1 upper stage from Xichang, though no official mission objectives, orbital data, or payload details have been disclosed. Like other Shiyan missions, its purpose is presumed to be experimental or technology-demonstration in nature, but information remains scarce due to the programs high level of secrecy, with most insights coming from independent trackers and spaceflight forums rather than official Chinese sources.

JDay 252 at 0047z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers a verified maneuver on COSMOS 2588 (64095). The maneuver occurred at 8Sep1503z (JDAY 251). This maneuver is possibly related to the previous maneuvers done over the last 48 hours.

The satellite maneuvered with a total delta v of 1.42 m/s, resulting in a total period increase of 1.7sec resulting in a final period of 94.16min. This maneuver appears to be increasing its period once more, with a total overall increase of 7.75sec period increase since the start of the sequence. These maneuvers do not appear to be station-keeping maneuvers and are not within the historical pattern of life for this object. Neighborhood is provided. Click link above to view products.

COSMOS 2588(64095) is a Russian satellite that supports military operations. The mission of COSMOS 2588 is on orbit inspection and earth observation. There is speculation that the satellite may have a kinetic weapon system aboard it.

The specifics of the first maneuver are: 
--Time of Maneuver: 8SEP1503z
--Delta V: 1.42 m/s
--Period Change: 1.7 secs
--Apogee Change: 2.11 km
--Perigee Change: 0.644 km
--Inclination Change: 0.0 degs

JDay 251 at 0621z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have detected a Photometric change on TJS-17 (63524). This change occurred between the solar phase angles of +30 to +103 and appeared to be up to 2 visual magnitude brighter in some regions. 

The cause of the change may be associated with unknown activity. No manoeuvres were detected, the satellite remains on ELSET, and no close approaches were observed during the photometric change window. This photometric variation is not consistent with the historical pattern of life for this object. Analysis is ongoing.

TJS-17 (63524) is in GEO and is currently at 164.4 E longitude and is drifting at 0.008 W per day. Neighborhood is provided. Click link above to view products.

TJS-17 (63524) is a Chinese satellite that supports military operations. The mission of TJS-17 is assessed to involve experimental GEO communications and signals intelligence technology.

Mission Summary:
The Chamran-1 research satellite, successfully launched on September 14, 2024, by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) using the Qaem-100 solid-fuel rocket, is a 60 kg domestically developed satellite placed into a 550 km low Earth orbit to advance Iran's space technology capabilities. Designed and built by Iran Electronics Industries (SAIran) in collaboration with the Aerospace Research Institute and private firms, its primary mission is to test hardware and software systems for validating orbital maneuvering technology, including altitude and phase adjustments, critical for future satellite constellations. Mission Summary:
The payload for this launch is speculated to be the Shiyan-29 (SY-29).  The SY-series is part of Chinas long-running Shiyan (Experimental) satellite series, which has been used since 2004 to test a wide range of space technologies, including rendezvous and proximity operations, Earth and space environment monitoring, and satellite servicing. SY-29 is reportedly launching around September 5, 2025, aboard a Chang Zheng-3C (CZ-3C) rocket with a YZ-1 upper stage from Xichang, though no official mission objectives, orbital data, or payload details have been disclosed. Like other Shiyan missions, its purpose is presumed to be experimental or technology-demonstration in nature, but information remains scarce due to the programs high level of secrecy, with most insights coming from independent trackers and spaceflight forums rather than official Chinese sources.
Source: RC

Mission Summary:
The payload for this launch is speculated to be the Shiyan-29 (SY-29).  The SY-series is part of Chinas long-running Shiyan (Experimental) satellite series, which has been used since 2004 to test a wide range of space technologies, including rendezvous and proximity operations, Earth and space environment monitoring, and satellite servicing. SY-29 is reportedly launching around September 5, 2025, aboard a Chang Zheng-3C (CZ-3C) rocket with a YZ-1 upper stage from Xichang, though no official mission objectives, orbital data, or payload details have been disclosed. Like other Shiyan missions, its purpose is presumed to be experimental or technology-demonstration in nature, but information remains scarce due to the programs high level of secrecy, with most insights coming from independent trackers and spaceflight forums rather than official Chinese sources.

JDAY 248, 0902Z

Mission Summary:
The Progress-M resupply missions, operated by Roscosmos, are a series of uncrewed cargo spacecraft launches designed to deliver essential supplies to the International Space Station (ISS), a role they have fulfilled since 2000. Derived from the Soviet-era Soyuz spacecraft, the Progress-M (including variants like Progress M1, M-M, and MS) carries up to 2,400 kg of cargo, including food, water, oxygen, fuel, and scientific equipment, to support the ISS crew and operations. Launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan using Soyuz rockets, these spacecraft use the automated Kurs docking system to autonomously dock at the stations aft port, typically the Zvezda service module, where they can remain for up to six months. In addition to delivering supplies, Progress-M spacecraft transfer propellant to the ISS, reboost the stations orbit to counter atmospheric drag, and dispose of waste by burning up during reentry. With over 170 missions flown by 2021, including notable deliveries like the Pirs, Poisk, and Prichal modules, the Progress-M series remains a cornerstone of ISS logistics, ensuring continuous support for crew and research

Space weather will be updated NLT 24 hours before launch

Mission Summary:
The Progress-M resupply missions, operated by Roscosmos, are a series of uncrewed cargo spacecraft launches designed to deliver essential supplies to the International Space Station (ISS), a role they have fulfilled since 2000. Derived from the Soviet-era Soyuz spacecraft, the Progress-M (including variants like Progress M1, M-M, and MS) carries up to 2,400 kg of cargo, including food, water, oxygen, fuel, and scientific equipment, to support the ISS crew and operations. Launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan using Soyuz rockets, these spacecraft use the automated Kurs docking system to autonomously dock at the stations aft port, typically the Zvezda service module, where they can remain for up to six months. In addition to delivering supplies, Progress-M spacecraft transfer propellant to the ISS, reboost the stations orbit to counter atmospheric drag, and dispose of waste by burning up during reentry. With over 170 missions flown by 2021, including notable deliveries like the Pirs, Poisk, and Prichal modules, the Progress-M series remains a cornerstone of ISS logistics, ensuring continuous support for crew and research

Space weather will be updated NLT 24 hours before launch

Mission Summary:
Russias GLONASS-K satellites are the third-generation spacecraft in the countrys Global Navigation Satellite System (GLONASS), designed to modernize and sustain Russias counterpart to the U.S. GPS network. Built by ISS Reshetnev, the unpressurized GLONASS-K series represents a major technological step forward from earlier Uragan designs, offering longer lifespans (up to 10 years), lighter structures, and improved signal capabilities. Each satellite broadcasts both legacy navigation signals and new CDMA signals to enhance accuracy, reliability, and compatibility with international GNSS systems. Operating primarily in medium Earth orbit at ~19,100 km altitude, GLONASS-K satellites play a central role in ensuring Russias autonomous global navigation and positioning capability, supporting both civilian and military applications while reducing dependence on foreign systems.
Source: RC

Mission Summary:
Luch Olymp-K is a Russian geostationary satellite built for the Russian Ministry of Defense and the Russian intelligence agency, FSB. Russian press reports indicate that the satellite may also be used by the Russian FSB for espionage and ELINT (including that of other satellites), in addition to Russian naval communications. During its first five years on orbit, Luch parked near more than a dozen commercial communications satellites for periods ranging from a few weeks to nine months, and typically close enough to be within the typical ground terminal uplink beam.

msgBody.Event_Description:
JDay 255 at 1630z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a maneuver on LUCH (OLYMP) (40258) occurring at 11Sep1454z (JDay 254).

The satellite maneuvered from 65.54deg E longitude with a delta-v of 0.06 m/s, resulting in an period change of +3.53sec to a final period of 1436.12min. This maneuver appears to be a station-keeping maneuver and is not within the historical pattern of life for this object.

Until now, LUCH (OLYMP) hasn't maneuvered since it left its longitude parking spot of ~18deg W longitude on 26Mar2025 and then parked at ~65deg E longitude on 23Aug2025. LUCH (OLYMP) currently has a close approach approximately every 24 hours with each continually growing in distance with a well tracked UCT that appears to be unstable. The last close approach was 12Sep0224z @ 32.21km with the next being 13Sep0214 @ 58.09km. Neighborhood of nearby objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver.

Luch (OLYMP) (40258) is a Russian satellite that supports military operations. The mission of Luch (OLYMP) is a military communications satellite with reported ELECTRONIC INTELLIGENCE (ELINT) function to spy on communications of other satellites.

The specifics of the maneuver are: 
--Time of Maneuver: 11Sep1454z
--Delta V: 0.06 m/s
--Period Change:  +3.53secs
--Apogee Change: +2.16 km
--Perigee Change: +0.13 km
--Inclination Change: +0.003 degs
--Current Drift Rate: 0.004 W deg/day

msgBody.Event_Description:
JDay 255 at 1615z:
  
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a maneuver on SJ-20 (44910) occurring at 0115z on 12 Sep (JDay 255), and indications of a possible maneuver at ~1340z on 12Sep.  Also, there were 2 photometric changes associated with the maneuvers.

The satellite maneuvered from 78.42 Degs E longitude with a delta-v of 00.70 m/s, resulting in an increase in westward drift rate of .25 W deg/day.  A review of historical plots indicated SJ-20 (44910) posted at ~ 73 deg longitude from June 2024 - May 2025 its possibly maneuvering to its historical location.

Neighborhood of nearby objects is attached showing there was a close approach to USA 211 (36108) on 12Sep at 0034zas a result of this maneuver. While sun angles were good at this time, SJ-20 was rapidly moving away from USA 211, and is continuing to do so. 
Click link above to view products.

This satellite has a history of body rolling sideways to perform large maneuvers which maybe a reason for the photometry changes. The change also coincided with a close approach with USA 211 (36108) at 12SEP0033z at 53.4km and SJ-20 had bad lighting to view USA 211. This photometric variation is indicative of large maneuver behavior for this satellite . Analysis is ongoing.

The satellite is in GEO and is currently at ~78.10 degs E longitude and is drifting at ~0.35 W deg/day. 
 
SJ-20 (44910) is a Chinese satellite that supports military operations. The mission of SJ-20 is high throughput communications, and technology testing and prototyping.
 
USA 211(36108) is a US satellite that supports military operations. The mission of USA 211 is communications.
  
The specifics of the maneuver are: 
--Time of Maneuver: 12Sep0115z
--Delta V: 0.70 m/s
--Period Change: -60.17 secs
--Apogee Change: -0.36 km
--Perigee Change: -38.88 km
--Inclination Change: +0.0029 degs
--Current Drift Rate: 0.33 W deg/day

Mission Summary:
Russias GLONASS-K satellites are the third-generation spacecraft in the countrys Global Navigation Satellite System (GLONASS), designed to modernize and sustain Russias counterpart to the U.S. GPS network. Built by ISS Reshetnev, the unpressurized GLONASS-K series represents a major technological step forward from earlier Uragan designs, offering longer lifespans (up to 10 years), lighter structures, and improved signal capabilities. Each satellite broadcasts both legacy navigation signals and new CDMA signals to enhance accuracy, reliability, and compatibility with international GNSS systems. Operating primarily in medium Earth orbit at ~19,100 km altitude, GLONASS-K satellites play a central role in ensuring Russias autonomous global navigation and positioning capability, supporting both civilian and military applications while reducing dependence on foreign systems.

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a maneuver on SJ-20 (44910) occurring at 0115z on 12 Sep (JDay 255), and indications of a possible maneuver at ~1340z on 12Sep.  Also, there were 2 photometric changes associated with the maneuvers.

The satellite maneuvered from 78.42 Degs E longitude with a delta-v of 00.70 m/s, resulting in an increase in westward drift rate of .25 W deg/day.  A review of historical plots indicated SJ-20 (44910) posted at ~ 73 deg longitude from June 2024 - May 2025 its possibly maneuvering to its historical location.

Neighborhood of nearby objects is attached showing there was a close approach to USA 211 (36108) on 12Sep at 0034zas a result of this maneuver. While sun angles were good at this time, SJ-20 was rapidly moving away from USA 211, and is continuing to do so. 
Click link above to view products.

This satellite has a history of body rolling sideways to perform large maneuvers which maybe a reason for the photometry changes. The change also coincided with a close approach with USA 211 (36108) at 12SEP0033z at 53.4km and SJ-20 had bad lighting to view USA 211. This photometric variation is indicative of large maneuver behavior for this satellite . Analysis is ongoing.

The satellite is in GEO and is currently at ~78.10 degs E longitude and is drifting at ~0.35 W deg/day.

Mission Summary:
Russias GLONASS-K satellites are the third-generation spacecraft in the countrys Global Navigation Satellite System (GLONASS), designed to modernize and sustain Russias counterpart to the U.S. GPS network. Built by ISS Reshetnev, the unpressurized GLONASS-K series represents a major technological step forward from earlier Uragan designs, offering longer lifespans (up to 10 years), lighter structures, and improved signal capabilities. Each satellite broadcasts both legacy navigation signals and new CDMA signals to enhance accuracy, reliability, and compatibility with international GNSS systems. Operating primarily in medium Earth orbit at ~19,100 km altitude, GLONASS-K satellites play a central role in ensuring Russias autonomous global navigation and positioning capability, supporting both civilian and military applications while reducing dependence on foreign systems.

Mission Summary:
Russias GLONASS-K satellites are the third-generation spacecraft in the countrys Global Navigation Satellite System (GLONASS), designed to modernize and sustain Russias counterpart to the U.S. GPS network. Built by ISS Reshetnev, the unpressurized GLONASS-K series represents a major technological step forward from earlier Uragan designs, offering longer lifespans (up to 10 years), lighter structures, and improved signal capabilities. Each satellite broadcasts both legacy navigation signals and new CDMA signals to enhance accuracy, reliability, and compatibility with international GNSS systems. Operating primarily in medium Earth orbit at ~19,100 km altitude, GLONASS-K satellites play a central role in ensuring Russias autonomous global navigation and positioning capability, supporting both civilian and military applications while reducing dependence on foreign systems.

Mission Summary:
The Progress-M resupply missions, operated by Roscosmos, are a series of uncrewed cargo spacecraft launches designed to deliver essential supplies to the International Space Station (ISS), a role they have fulfilled since 2000. Derived from the Soviet-era Soyuz spacecraft, the Progress-M (including variants like Progress M1, M-M, and MS) carries up to 2,400 kg of cargo, including food, water, oxygen, fuel, and scientific equipment, to support the ISS crew and operations. Launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan using Soyuz rockets, these spacecraft use the automated Kurs docking system to autonomously dock at the stations aft port, typically the Zvezda service module, where they can remain for up to six months. In addition to delivering supplies, Progress-M spacecraft transfer propellant to the ISS, reboost the stations orbit to counter atmospheric drag, and dispose of waste by burning up during reentry. With over 170 missions flown by 2021, including notable deliveries like the Pirs, Poisk, and Prichal modules, the Progress-M series remains a cornerstone of ISS logistics, ensuring continuous support for crew and research

Mission Summary:
The Progress-M resupply missions, operated by Roscosmos, are a series of uncrewed cargo spacecraft launches designed to deliver essential supplies to the International Space Station (ISS), a role they have fulfilled since 2000. Derived from the Soviet-era Soyuz spacecraft, the Progress-M (including variants like Progress M1, M-M, and MS) carries up to 2,400 kg of cargo, including food, water, oxygen, fuel, and scientific equipment, to support the ISS crew and operations. Launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan using Soyuz rockets, these spacecraft use the automated Kurs docking system to autonomously dock at the stations aft port, typically the Zvezda service module, where they can remain for up to six months. In addition to delivering supplies, Progress-M spacecraft transfer propellant to the ISS, reboost the stations orbit to counter atmospheric drag, and dispose of waste by burning up during reentry. With over 170 missions flown by 2021, including notable deliveries like the Pirs, Poisk, and Prichal modules, the Progress-M series remains a cornerstone of ISS logistics, ensuring continuous support for crew and research

Mission Summary:
TJS-3 is a Chinese GEO satellite of unknown purpose. Due to the lack of available information it is thought to have a military mission, possibly SIGINT or early warning. The satellite is thought to have a multi-frequency and high speed communications payload.TJS-3 was launched in December 2018 and entered GEO after a few days. A separated object was initially thought to be a chemical apogee kick stage, but this object has maneuvered after separation and is considered a subsatellite.
Source: JB and https://space.skyrocket.de/doc_sdat/tjs-3.htm

JDay 258 at 0610z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have detected a Photometric change on TJS-3 (43874). This change occurred between the solar phase angles of 75 to 78 and appeared to be ~0.5 visual magnitude brighter. 

The cause of the change may be a close approach with Beidou 11 (38091) at 14 SEP 2350z at 24km. TJS-3 had good lighting to view Beidou 11. This photometric variation is approximately consistent with the historical pattern of life for this object. Analysis is ongoing.
 
The satellite is in GEO and is currently at 58.93 degs E longitude and is drifting at 0.0046 W deg/day. Neighborhood is provided. Click link above to view products.

msgBody.Email_Subject: NOTSO - Maneuver / 63924 / TJS-19 / GEO - 3c28_15Sep-1538Z - TACREP Notification
msgBody.Remarks:
JDAY 258, 1447z

Mission Summary:
The Tongxin Jishu Shiyan-19 (TJS-19) satellite, identified by NORAD ID 63924, is a classified Chinese experimental spacecraft launched on May 12, 2025, at approximately 18:09 UTC from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center (LC3) aboard a Long March 3C/G2 rocket (Y7), marking the vehicle's seventh flight and China's 25th orbital mission of the year; developed by the Shanghai Academy of Spaceflight Technology (SAST) under the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC), TJS-19 was inserted into a geosynchronous transfer orbit (GTO) with an apogee of around 35,800 km, perigee of 200 km, and inclination of 28.5, from which it used onboard propulsion to reach geostationary orbit (GEO) at approximately 36,000 km altitude for operations; officially described as a communication technology experiment satellite primarily for verifying multi-band, high-speed satellite communication technologies, including data transmission, radio, and television services, the mission aligns with the opaque TJS series' pattern of vague disclosures and last-minute airspace closures, leading Western analysts to speculate on underlying military objectives such as signals intelligence (SIGINT), early warning missile detection, or satellite inspection activities to support the People's Liberation Army (PLA), potentially as part of the Qianshao-3 or Huoyan-1 subclasses; with an estimated mass of 1,0002,500 kg on an SAST DFH-4 or similar bus, TJS-19 contributes to China's expanding GEO constellation of 17 active TJS satellites (skipping TJS-8 and TJS-18), enhancing strategic space domain awareness amid growing counterspace demonstrations, and remains operational as of September 2025 with no public images or detailed results released.
Source: RC

JDay 258 at 1745z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a maneuver on CHAMRAN-1 (61072) occurring at 14Sep/1204z on JDAY 257.

CHAMRAN-1 maneuvered with a Delta-V of 1.85 m/s, increasing its Period by 2.83 secs by raising its Perigee by 1.88 km and its Apogee by 2.68 km and shifting its RAAN by -3.38 deg. This maneuver does not appear to be a station-keeping maneuver but is within the historical pattern of life for this object. Neighborhood is provided. Click link above to view products.

Since 17 August, CHAMRAN-1 has conducted multiple oppositional Period changes along with several small plane changes. Close approaches to in-plane objects are regular and radial fly-bys have occurred with planar objects QAEM 100 R/B (61071), Object H (51953), and MEGSAT 1 (26546) and in several instances were co-timed. This most recent maneuver appears to have happened immediately following a fly-by with Object H. CHAMRAN-1 will have an upcoming close approach with QAEM 100 R/B on 19 Sep1853z at 34kms with good lighting and is currently very well Inclination matched. While CHAMRAN-1 appears to be Cross-Track hopping around the R/B, worth noting that of the objects, it is most well-phased with Object H despite a larger Inclination delta. Primary object continues to be the QAEM-100 R/B.

CHAMRAN-1 (61072) is an Iranian satellite that supports civil/other operations. The mission of CHAMRAN-1 is a propulsion technology test satellite. The CHAMRAN-1 was launched on a QAEM-100 rocket on 14 Sep 2024 and QAEM-100 R/B (61071) is associated with this launch.

MEGSAT 1 (26546) is an Italian satellite that supports civil/other operations. The mission of MEGSAT 1 is a Scientific Atmospheric Research Technology test satellite.

Object H is associated with a Chinese launch on 5 March 2022 and is speculated to be the CZ-2C R/B. Nothing further is known.

The specifics of the maneuver are: 
--Time of Maneuver: 14Sep1204z
--Delta V: 1.85 m/s
--Period Change: 2.83 secs

--Perigee Change: 1.87 km

msgBody.Remarks:
JDAY 258, 1447z

Mission Summary:
The Tongxin Jishu Shiyan-19 (TJS-19) satellite, identified by NORAD ID 63924, is a classified Chinese experimental spacecraft launched on May 12, 2025, at approximately 18:09 UTC from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center (LC3) aboard a Long March 3C/G2 rocket (Y7), marking the vehicle's seventh flight and China's 25th orbital mission of the year; developed by the Shanghai Academy of Spaceflight Technology (SAST) under the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC), TJS-19 was inserted into a geosynchronous transfer orbit (GTO) with an apogee of around 35,800 km, perigee of 200 km, and inclination of 28.5, from which it used onboard propulsion to reach geostationary orbit (GEO) at approximately 36,000 km altitude for operations; officially described as a communication technology experiment satellite primarily for verifying multi-band, high-speed satellite communication technologies, including data transmission, radio, and television services, the mission aligns with the opaque TJS series' pattern of vague disclosures and last-minute airspace closures, leading Western analysts to speculate on underlying military objectives such as signals intelligence (SIGINT), early warning missile detection, or satellite inspection activities to support the People's Liberation Army (PLA), potentially as part of the Qianshao-3 or Huoyan-1 subclasses; with an estimated mass of 1,0002,500 kg on an SAST DFH-4 or similar bus, TJS-19 contributes to China's expanding GEO constellation of 17 active TJS satellites (skipping TJS-8 and TJS-18), enhancing strategic space domain awareness amid growing counterspace demonstrations, and remains operational as of September 2025 with no public images or detailed results released.
Source: RC

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers detected a possible maneuver on TJS-19 (63924), occurring around 15Sep0758z, JDay 258.

The satellite was located at 141.13 degs E longitude. Based off of initial indications it appears it decreased it's orbital period by ~9.1 seconds and appears to be associated with monthly POL station keeping. Click link above to view products. Analysis is ongoing.

TJS-19 (63924) is a Chinese satellite that supports military operations. The mission of TJS-19 is thought to be high-speed internet communications but also undeclared functions as well such as experimental technology.

JDAY 258, 1447z

Mission Summary:
The Tongxin Jishu Shiyan-19 (TJS-19) satellite, identified by NORAD ID 63924, is a classified Chinese experimental spacecraft launched on May 12, 2025, at approximately 18:09 UTC from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center (LC3) aboard a Long March 3C/G2 rocket (Y7), marking the vehicle's seventh flight and China's 25th orbital mission of the year; developed by the Shanghai Academy of Spaceflight Technology (SAST) under the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC), TJS-19 was inserted into a geosynchronous transfer orbit (GTO) with an apogee of around 35,800 km, perigee of 200 km, and inclination of 28.5, from which it used onboard propulsion to reach geostationary orbit (GEO) at approximately 36,000 km altitude for operations; officially described as a communication technology experiment satellite primarily for verifying multi-band, high-speed satellite communication technologies, including data transmission, radio, and television services, the mission aligns with the opaque TJS series' pattern of vague disclosures and last-minute airspace closures, leading Western analysts to speculate on underlying military objectives such as signals intelligence (SIGINT), early warning missile detection, or satellite inspection activities to support the People's Liberation Army (PLA), potentially as part of the Qianshao-3 or Huoyan-1 subclasses; with an estimated mass of 1,0002,500 kg on an SAST DFH-4 or similar bus, TJS-19 contributes to China's expanding GEO constellation of 17 active TJS satellites (skipping TJS-8 and TJS-18), enhancing strategic space domain awareness amid growing counterspace demonstrations, and remains operational as of September 2025 with no public images or detailed results released.
Source: RC

JDAY 259 at 0245z
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have detected a Photometric change on TJS-3 (43874). This change occurred between the solar phase angles of 75 to 77 and appeared to be 0.5 visual magnitude dimmer. 
 
The photometric change has placed TJS-3 back to normal pattern of life after the close approach of Beidou 11 (38091), please see below. Analysis is ongoing.
 
The satellite is in GEO and is currently at 58.95 degs E longitude and is geo-stationary. Neighborhood is provided. Click link above to view products
 
TJS-3 (43874) is a Chinese satellite that supports military operations. The mission of TJS-3 is communications, signals Intelligence but may have secondary missile defense/early warning/space ELINT role.
 
Beidou 11 (38091) is a Chinese satellite that supports military operations. The mission of Beidou 11 is a navigation satellite.

JDay 259 at 1425z:

JDay 259 at 1835z: 

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a maneuver on SY-12 02 (50322) occurring at 16Sep0747z (JDay 259). 
The satellite maneuvered at 136.59 deg E longitude with a delta-v of 0.07 m/s, resulting in an decrease in westward drift rate to a driftrate of 0.5 W degs/day.
The effect of the maneuver resulted in a slight increase of min. distance  between JCSAT 17 and SY-12 02 by increasing the min distance by 10km.
Neighborhood of nearby objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver.

Notable upcoming close approaches: 
JCSAT 17 (45245) on 17Sep1250z (JDay 260) at 34.56km, 
USA 153 (26575) on 20Sep1640z (JDay 261) at 51.06km and 
USA 283 (43339) on 21Sep2034z (JDay 262) at 78.32km. 

The specifics of the maneuver are: 
--Time of Maneuver: 16Sep0747z
--Delta V: 0.07 m/s 
--Period Change: -7.27 secs 
--Apogee Change: -4.42 km 
--Perigee Change: -0.32 km 
--Inclination Change: 0.0024 degs 
--Current Drift Rate: 0.51 W deg/day

JDay 260 at 0440z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have processed initial states for four objects from the launch of a LM-2C/YZ-1S (94160) from Jiuquan, China occurring at 0106z 16 SEP, carrying Objects A (65617), B (65618), C (65619) and D (65620). Currently, Object E (65621) is untracked and requires more observations.
Based on current information the satellites are currently in LEO with orbital characteristics of Inc: 50.00 deg and RAAN: 334.58 deg to 334.74 deg.

msgBody.Remarks:
JDAY 260, 1843z

Mission Summary:
The name Shijian translates to Practice and is a line of missions usually used to carry out scientific experiments and technical verification. Chinese state media describes the satellite as 'mainly used for scientific experiments and technical verification'. Its exact purpose and use have been kept a secret. Further complicating matters is the fact that initial reports after launch from both China's main space contractor and state media Xinhua listed two additional satellites, Shiyan 22A and 22B, as payloads aboard the launch. An updated story from Xinhua a day later omitted reference to the latter pair. There is speculation that SJ-23 may attempt to replicate space debris removal experiments similar to seen with SJ-21. 
Source: EJS (SpaceDen)

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have detected a Photometric change on SJ-23 (55131).

msgBody.Remarks:
JDAY 260, 1843z

Mission Summary:
The name Shijian translates to Practice and is a line of missions usually used to carry out scientific experiments and technical verification. Chinese state media describes the satellite as 'mainly used for scientific experiments and technical verification'. Its exact purpose and use have been kept a secret. Further complicating matters is the fact that initial reports after launch from both China's main space contractor and state media Xinhua listed two additional satellites, Shiyan 22A and 22B, as payloads aboard the launch. An updated story from Xinhua a day later omitted reference to the latter pair. There is speculation that SJ-23 may attempt to replicate space debris removal experiments similar to seen with SJ-21. 
Source: EJS (SpaceDen)

Mission Summary:
The name Shijian translates to Practice and is a line of missions usually used to carry out scientific experiments and technical verification. Chinese state media describes the satellite as 'mainly used for scientific experiments and technical verification'. Its exact purpose and use have been kept a secret. Further complicating matters is the fact that initial reports after launch from both China's main space contractor and state media Xinhua listed two additional satellites, Shiyan 22A and 22B, as payloads aboard the launch. An updated story from Xinhua a day later omitted reference to the latter pair. There is speculation that SJ-23 may attempt to replicate space debris removal experiments similar to seen with SJ-21. 
Source: EJS (SpaceDen)

JDAY 261, 1446Z

Mission Summary
Shiyan-12-02 is a Chinese experimental/high-orbit satellite launched on 23 December 2021 aboard a Chang Zheng-7A (Long March 7A) rocket from Wenchang. It is one half of the twin Shiyan-12-01 / Shiyan-12-02 pair (codename HOTS  High Orbit Test Satellite) deployed to geosynchronous or near-geosynchronous orbit. Its publicized purpose is space environment studies and related technology demonstration; observers believe it may perform functions such as space weather monitoring, orbital calibration, drift-and-station-keeping tests, and possibly even inspection or rendezvousproximity operations (i.e., observing other GEO satellites). Its orbit is GEO drift / inclined GEO (~35,800 km altitude, small inclination), and its behavior (including periodic maneuvers and drift reversals) suggests its being used to test high-orbit satellite control, drift management, and possibly interactions or relative positioning with other satellites in GEO. 
Source: RC

SUMMARY: JDay 261 at 2120z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified maneuver on TJS-13 (62188) occurring ~02Sep2154z. 

TJS-13 conducted a significant maneuver to change apsidal/SMA characteristics. While the observations are not easily used, this pattern does match orbit size changes undertaken by both SHIYAN-10 and SHIYAN-10-02 in November and December of last year.

The satellite maneuvered with a delta v of 63.01 m/s, resulting in a 0.83 period decrease, perigee increase of 350.59 km, and apogee decrease of 351.18 km. Neighborhood is provided. Click link above to view products.
 
TJS-13 (62188) is a Chinese satellite in an elliptical orbit that supports military operations. The mission of TJS-13 is experimental signals intelligence and possibly early warning and communications.
 
The specifics of the maneuver are: 
--Time of Maneuver: ~02Sep2154z
--Delta V: 61.32 m/s
--Period Change: -0.74 secs
--Apogee Change: -352.58 km
--Perigee Change:  +352.08 km
--Inclination Change: +0.01 degs

JDAY 262, 1107Z

Mission Summary
Shijian-17 (SJ-17, NORAD 41838, COSPAR 2016-065A), launched on November 3, 2016, aboard a Long March 5 rocket from China's Wenchang Satellite Launch Center, is an experimental geostationary satellite developed by the China Academy of Space Technology (CAST) under the National University of Defense Technology's "Tianfang-1" project, utilizing an improved DFH-3B bus platform with a mass of approximately 4,000 kg. Positioned in geostationary Earth orbit (GEO) via direct insertion using the YZ-2 upper stage, its primary mission is to demonstrate advanced technologies for future Chinese satellites, including electric propulsion systems (Hall-effect and ion thrusters) for enhanced orbital maneuverability, high-efficiency solar array cells, composite load-bearing structures, solid composite lithium-ion batteries, temperature and vibration control systems, guidance/navigation/control (GNC) enhancements, and high-orbit GNSS-based navigation techniques. Equipped with China's first on-board robotic arm, SJ-17 supports space-based optical observation, communications services, and potential debris manipulation, serving as a testbed for space situational awareness, on-orbit inspection, and satellite servicing. Its frequent orbital relocations (37.7E to 180E), close-proximity operations (as near as 1.67 km to Chinasat 6A in 2017 and 55 km to other satellites), and rendezvous with inactive assets like Chinasat 5A have raised international concerns about dual-use counterspace capabilities, including potential satellite grappling or kinetic attacks, as noted in U.S. Department of Defense reports and USSPACECOM statements since 2021. As of September 2025, SJ-17 remains active in GEO, contributing to China's broader space ambitions, including programs like Shijian-25 (launched January 2025 for refueling tests), while its maneuvers suggest roles in both debris management and strategic space superiority.
Source: RC

SJ-17 (41838) is a Chinese Communications technology demonstration satellite that supports commercial operations and also carries a robotic arm.

Mission Summary
Shijian-17 (SJ-17, NORAD 41838, COSPAR 2016-065A), launched on November 3, 2016, aboard a Long March 5 rocket from China's Wenchang Satellite Launch Center, is an experimental geostationary satellite developed by the China Academy of Space Technology (CAST) under the National University of Defense Technology's "Tianfang-1" project, utilizing an improved DFH-3B bus platform with a mass of approximately 4,000 kg. Positioned in geostationary Earth orbit (GEO) via direct insertion using the YZ-2 upper stage, its primary mission is to demonstrate advanced technologies for future Chinese satellites, including electric propulsion systems (Hall-effect and ion thrusters) for enhanced orbital maneuverability, high-efficiency solar array cells, composite load-bearing structures, solid composite lithium-ion batteries, temperature and vibration control systems, guidance/navigation/control (GNC) enhancements, and high-orbit GNSS-based navigation techniques. Equipped with China's first on-board robotic arm, SJ-17 supports space-based optical observation, communications services, and potential debris manipulation, serving as a testbed for space situational awareness, on-orbit inspection, and satellite servicing. Its frequent orbital relocations (37.7E to 180E), close-proximity operations (as near as 1.67 km to Chinasat 6A in 2017 and 55 km to other satellites), and rendezvous with inactive assets like Chinasat 5A have raised international concerns about dual-use counterspace capabilities, including potential satellite grappling or kinetic attacks, as noted in U.S. Department of Defense reports and USSPACECOM statements since 2021. As of September 2025, SJ-17 remains active in GEO, contributing to China's broader space ambitions, including programs like Shijian-25 (launched January 2025 for refueling tests), while its maneuvers suggest roles in both debris management and strategic space superiority.

Mission Summary:
Russias GLONASS-K satellites are the third-generation spacecraft in the countrys Global Navigation Satellite System (GLONASS), designed to modernize and sustain Russias counterpart to the U.S. GPS network. Built by ISS Reshetnev, the unpressurized GLONASS-K series represents a major technological step forward from earlier Uragan designs, offering longer lifespans (up to 10 years), lighter structures, and improved signal capabilities. Each satellite broadcasts both legacy navigation signals and new CDMA signals to enhance accuracy, reliability, and compatibility with international GNSS systems. Operating primarily in medium Earth orbit at ~19,100 km altitude, GLONASS-K satellites play a central role in ensuring Russias autonomous global navigation and positioning capability, supporting both civilian and military applications while reducing dependence on foreign systems.

Mission Summary:
Russias GLONASS-K satellites are the third-generation spacecraft in the countrys Global Navigation Satellite System (GLONASS), designed to modernize and sustain Russias counterpart to the U.S. GPS network. Built by ISS Reshetnev, the unpressurized GLONASS-K series represents a major technological step forward from earlier Uragan designs, offering longer lifespans (up to 10 years), lighter structures, and improved signal capabilities. Each satellite broadcasts both legacy navigation signals and new CDMA signals to enhance accuracy, reliability, and compatibility with international GNSS systems. Operating primarily in medium Earth orbit at ~19,100 km altitude, GLONASS-K satellites play a central role in ensuring Russias autonomous global navigation and positioning capability, supporting both civilian and military applications while reducing dependence on foreign systems.

JDAY 261, 1446Z

Mission Summary
Shiyan-12-02 is a Chinese experimental/high-orbit satellite launched on 23 December 2021 aboard a Chang Zheng-7A (Long March 7A) rocket from Wenchang. It is one half of the twin Shiyan-12-01 / Shiyan-12-02 pair (codename HOTS  High Orbit Test Satellite) deployed to geosynchronous or near-geosynchronous orbit. Its publicized purpose is space environment studies and related technology demonstration; observers believe it may perform functions such as space weather monitoring, orbital calibration, drift-and-station-keeping tests, and possibly even inspection or rendezvousproximity operations (i.e., observing other GEO satellites). Its orbit is GEO drift / inclined GEO (~35,800 km altitude, small inclination), and its behavior (including periodic maneuvers and drift reversals) suggests its being used to test high-orbit satellite control, drift management, and possibly interactions or relative positioning with other satellites in GEO. 
Source: RC

msgBody.Remarks:
JDAY 261, 1446Z

Mission Summary
Shiyan-12-02 is a Chinese experimental/high-orbit satellite launched on 23 December 2021 aboard a Chang Zheng-7A (Long March 7A) rocket from Wenchang. It is one half of the twin Shiyan-12-01 / Shiyan-12-02 pair (codename HOTS  High Orbit Test Satellite) deployed to geosynchronous or near-geosynchronous orbit. Its publicized purpose is space environment studies and related technology demonstration; observers believe it may perform functions such as space weather monitoring, orbital calibration, drift-and-station-keeping tests, and possibly even inspection or rendezvousproximity operations (i.e., observing other GEO satellites). Its orbit is GEO drift / inclined GEO (~35,800 km altitude, small inclination), and its behavior (including periodic maneuvers and drift reversals) suggests its being used to test high-orbit satellite control, drift management, and possibly interactions or relative positioning with other satellites in GEO. 
Source: RC

JDay 265 at 1550z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have detected a Photometric change on COSMOS-2589 (64467). This change occurred between the solar phase angles of -111 to -98 and appeared to be ~1.7 visual magnitude brighter. However in that time frame there were 4 instances, occurring 20 minutes apart, of the object peaking brightness then returning to Pattern of Life brightness in essence going up bright and dim during that phase angle.  This pattern was also observed in July 2025 during a close approach with OBJECT C (64527).
 
The cause of the change may be associated with a close approach with OBJECT C at 22Sep1222z at 23km and COSMOS 2589 had bad lighting to view OBJECT C. This photometric variation is not consistent with the historical pattern of life for this object. Analysis is ongoing.
 
The satellite is in HEO and is currently at 121.05 degs E longitude and is drifting 0.09deg/day E. Neighborhood is provided. Click link above to view products

JDay 265 at 1910z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified 3 maneuvers on Khayyam (53370), occurring on 21Sep at 0246z, 1559z, and 1902z. 

During the first maneuver, the satellite performed a delta v of 0.15 m/s, resulting in a period increase of 0.11 sec. During the second maneuver, the satellite performed a delta v of 3.67 m/s resulting in a period increase of 0.32 sec. Finally, during the third maneuver , the satellite performed a delta v of 0.15 m/s which also raised the period by 0.19 sec.

These maneuvers appear to be station-keeping maneuvers and within the historical pattern of life for this object, however we expect an additional period increase in the next few days to raise the period to the expected 94.4 minutes. Neighborhood is provided. Click link above to view products.

Khayyam is close to an Argentinian satellite  Nusat-38 (56202), another Earth observation satellite.

Khayyam (53370) is an (Iranian) satellite that supports military operations. The mission of Khayyam is Earth observation and reconnaissance.

JDay 265 at 2014z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have detected a Photometric change on CHINASAT-6C (44067). This change occurred between the solar phase angles of -50 to -100 and appeared to be 3 visual magnitudes brighter. 

The cause of the change could be the effect of the fall equinox season. Additionally, this could be satellite behavior for dealing with the effects of eclipse season. This photometric variation is consistent with the historical pattern of life for this object during both spring and fall equinox periods. Analysis is ongoing.

Mission Summary
China's Geely Future Mobility Constellation, also known as GEESATCOM and developed by Geespacea subsidiary of Zhejiang Geely Holding Groupaims to establish a low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite network comprising up to 240 satellites to deliver global satellite Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity, high-precision positioning, space-based communication, and remote sensing services, with a primary focus on enhancing intelligent mobility ecosystems for vehicles, including advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), autonomous driving, vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication, and fleet management for logistics and public transportation. The constellation's first phase targets deploying 72 satellites by the end of 2025 to achieve near-global coverage excluding polar regions, enabling applications in smart cities, environmental monitoring (such as maritime debris detection and water quality assessment), low-altitude transportation, emergency communications, and marine fisheries, while integrating aerospace technology with Geely's automotive innovations to support brands like Zeekr and foster broader commercial opportunities in consumer electronics and unmanned systems.

msgBody.Remarks:
JDAY 266, 1309z

Mission Summary:
The communications technology test satellite number 10, or TJS-10 is a Chinese geostationary satellite likely with a technological mission, but may be equipped with a military support payload. The purpose may be tests of multi-band, high-speed satellite communication technology. Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have detected a Photometric change on COSMOS-2589 (64467). This change occurred between the solar phase angles of -111 to -98 and appeared to be ~1.7 visual magnitude brighter. However in that time frame there were 4 instances, occurring 20 minutes apart, of the object peaking brightness then returning to Pattern of Life brightness in essence going up bright and dim during that phase angle. Mission Summary
China's Geely Future Mobility Constellation, also known as GEESATCOM and developed by Geespacea subsidiary of Zhejiang Geely Holding Groupaims to establish a low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite network comprising up to 240 satellites to deliver global satellite Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity, high-precision positioning, space-based communication, and remote sensing services, with a primary focus on enhancing intelligent mobility ecosystems for vehicles, including advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), autonomous driving, vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication, and fleet management for logistics and public transportation. The constellation's first phase targets deploying 72 satellites by the end of 2025 to achieve near-global coverage excluding polar regions, enabling applications in smart cities, environmental monitoring (such as maritime debris detection and water quality assessment), low-altitude transportation, emergency communications, and marine fisheries, while integrating aerospace technology with Geely's automotive innovations to support brands like Zeekr and foster broader commercial opportunities in consumer electronics and unmanned systems.

JDay 267 at 1015z:
 
Based on available PAIR data, JCO providers have indicated a successful launch of a Smart Dragon 3 (94501) from Yellow Sea Launch Area, China on JDay 267 occurring at 0756z, carrying Geely 60A-L (94502) satellites and Shikongxing 01 (94503). Based on current information, the satellite is likely to be LEO with orbital characteristics of 49.99 inclination and 99.23 RAAN.  COCO is provided. Click link above to view products.

The mission of Geely 06A-L, part of GEESATCOM, is likely to establish a low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite network for civilian use, delivering high-precision positioning, space-based communication, and remote sensing services, focusing on advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), autonomous driving, vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication, and fleet management for logistics and public transportation

Shikongxing 01 (94503) is an experimental satellite owned by Peking University. The term "Shikongxing" can be translated to "Spatio-temporal Star," which suggests its purpose is likely related to research in geographic information science or a similar field.

Mission Summary:
Shiyan 12-02 (NORAD ID 50322), part of China's experimental Shiyan satellite series, is a geosynchronous test satellite launched on December 23, 2021, at 07:50 UTC from the Wenchang Satellite Launch Center aboard a Long March 7A rocket alongside its twin Shiyan 12-01 (50321) and the rocket's upper stage, with the mission designated as 2021-129B. Orbiting at approximately 35,796 km altitude with a 2.09 inclination, the satellitedeveloped by the China Academy of Space Technology (CAST)serves an undisclosed purpose typical of the Shiyan program, likely involving technology demonstrations such as sensor trials, communications subsystems, environmental monitoring, or potential rendezvous proximity operations (RPO) in high orbit, as evidenced by similar satellites in the series that have conducted orbital maneuvers and sub-satellite releases.  The satellite's high maneuverability and its close-proximity operations with other satellites in geostationary orbit have been noted, leading to speculation that it is a counterpart to the U.S. Space Force's Geosynchronous Space Situational Awareness Program (GSSAP) satellites.

JDay 246 at 1310z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a manoeuvre on Shiyan 12-02 (50322) occurring around 0101z on the 24th September 2025 & JDAY 246. 

The satellite maneuvered from 132.48 degs E longitude with a delta-v of 0.12 m/s, resulting in a increase in westward drift to 0.558 W degs. Due to the maneuver the close approach with JCSAT 9 (29045) has increased from 26km to 48km on 25Sep 0825Z.

This manoeuvre does not appear to be a station-keeping manoeuvre more so a drift keep maneuver and is within the historical pattern of life for this object which is often observed to keep a greater than 30km distance between close approaches.

Neighbourhood of nearby objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this manoeuvre.

Shiyan 12-02 (50322) is a Chinese satellite that supports military operations. The mission of Shiyan 12-02 the mission of the satellite is for "space environment exploration and related technology tests" however, it is suspected that it is actually a military test satellite.

JCSAT 9 (29045) is a Japanese satellite that supports commercial operations. The mission of JCSAT 9 is to support commercial communications.

--Time of Manoeuvre: 24Sept0101z
--Delta V: 0.12 m/s
--Period Change: 8.56 secs
--Apogee Change: 1.323 km

China's Geely Future Mobility Constellation, also known as GEESATCOM and developed by Geespacea subsidiary of Zhejiang Geely Holding Groupaims to establish a low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite network comprising up to 240 satellites to deliver global satellite Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity, high-precision positioning, space-based communication, and remote sensing services, with a primary focus on enhancing intelligent mobility ecosystems for vehicles, including advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), autonomous driving, vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication, and fleet management for logistics and public transportation. Mission Summary
China's Geely Future Mobility Constellation, also known as GEESATCOM and developed by Geespacea subsidiary of Zhejiang Geely Holding Groupaims to establish a low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite network comprising up to 240 satellites to deliver global satellite Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity, high-precision positioning, space-based communication, and remote sensing services, with a primary focus on enhancing intelligent mobility ecosystems for vehicles, including advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), autonomous driving, vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication, and fleet management for logistics and public transportation. The constellation's first phase targets deploying 72 satellites by the end of 2025 to achieve near-global coverage excluding polar regions, enabling applications in smart cities, environmental monitoring (such as maritime debris detection and water quality assessment), low-altitude transportation, emergency communications, and marine fisheries, while integrating aerospace technology with Geely's automotive innovations to support brands like Zeekr and foster broader commercial opportunities in consumer electronics and unmanned systems.

msgBody.Email_Subject: NOTSO - Maneuver / 55131 / SJ-23 / GEO - fca7_26Sep-0901Z - TACREP Notification
msgBody.Remarks:
JDAY 269, 0702Z

Mission Summary
Shijian-23 (catalog number 55131, international designation 2023-002A), launched by China on January 9, 2023, aboard a Long March 7A rocket from the Wenchang Satellite Launch Center, represents a key mission in the nation's Shijian experimental satellite series aimed at advancing space technology and scientific research. As part of this classified program, the satellite was deployed into a geostationary transfer orbit, from which it utilized onboard propulsion to reach geosynchronous orbit, enabling extended operations for up to 15 years based on the DFH-4E satellite bus platform. Its primary objectives encompass conducting undisclosed scientific experiments and verifying advanced technical capabilities, potentially including innovations in communications, space environment monitoring, or rendezvous and proximity operations, consistent with the series' historical focus on practical applications for future missions like those in the China High-resolution Earth Observation System (CHEOS).
Source: RC

JDay 269 at 0709z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a maneuver on SJ-23 (55131) occurring at 0242z on 25Sep2025 (JDay 268).
The satellite maneuvered from 32.698deg E longitude with a delta-v of 0.0084 m/s, resulting in a decrease in westward drift rate from -0.693 W deg/day to -0.687 W deg/day. This maneuver does not appear to be a station-keeping maneuver and is within the historical pattern of life for this object. Neighborhood of nearby objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver.

SJ-23 (55131) is a Chinese satellite that supports military operations. The mission of SJ-23 is to serve as a communications and experimental technology demonstration satellite

msgBody.Remarks:
JDAY 269, 1315z

SJ 25 (Shijian 25) is a Chinese experimental satellite servicing vehicle, which aims to advance critical technologies for on-orbit refueling and extending satellite lifespans. It was launched in January 2025 on a LM-3B rocket and is designed to validate on orbit space debris reduction technology.
Source: TAB

The SJ-21 (Shijian-21) satellite is a key component of Chinas Shijian series, a program of experimental satellites aimed at advancing space technologies for the Peoples Republic of China. Officially focused on space debris mitigation, SJ-21 demonstrated sophisticated rendezvous and proximity operations (RPO) by interacting with the defunct Beidou-2 G2 navigation satellite. After approaching and matching its orbit, SJ-21 docked with Beidou-2 G2 in late December 2021, a maneuver tracked by space situational awareness firms like COMSPOC and ExoAnalytic Solutions. It then executed a significant engine burn on January 22, 2022, towing the defunct satellite 3,000 kilometers above the geostationary orbit (GEO) beltfar beyond the typical 300-kilometer graveyard orbitbefore undocking on January 26, 2022, and returning to GEO. This RPO capability highlights Chinas progress in on-orbit servicing and debris management, testing precise orbital maneuvering, close-proximity operations, and satellite manipulation, potentially via robotic arms or other mechanisms. Within the broader Shijian program, such activities refine operational practices and optimize technologies, distinguishing it from experimental series like Shiyan, which focus on initial technology testing.
Source: TAB

Mission Summary:
Russias GLONASS-K satellites are the third-generation spacecraft in the countrys Global Navigation Satellite System (GLONASS), designed to modernize and sustain Russias counterpart to the U.S. GPS network. Built by ISS Reshetnev, the unpressurized GLONASS-K series represents a major technological step forward from earlier Uragan designs, offering longer lifespans (up to 10 years), lighter structures, and improved signal capabilities. Each satellite broadcasts both legacy navigation signals and new CDMA signals to enhance accuracy, reliability, and compatibility with international GNSS systems. Operating primarily in medium Earth orbit at ~19,100 km altitude, GLONASS-K satellites play a central role in ensuring Russias autonomous global navigation and positioning capability, supporting both civilian and military applications while reducing dependence on foreign systems.

JDAY 268, 1100Z

Mission Summary:
The expected payload is the Yaogan-42C, third and likely final satellite in the 42 series.  The two previous Yagoan-42 satellites orbit at ~500km, 35 degree inclination.  It remains unclear the specific purpose/mission/function of these satellites.

The Yaogan ("Remote Sensing") series is a family of Chinese satellites developed and operated by the People's Liberation Army (PLA) Strategic Support Force, primarily for military reconnaissance and intelligence purposes. Initiated in 2006, the series encompasses over 150 satellites (as of September 2025) and includes a variety of missions such as optical imaging, synthetic aperture radar (SAR), electronic intelligence (ELINT), and ocean surveillance. Officially described by China as supporting "scientific research, land resource surveys, agricultural development, and disaster prevention," the series is widely recognized by Western analysts as a cornerstone of PLA's space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities, with applications in military targeting, maritime monitoring, and signal geolocation.
Source: TRB
