msgBody.Remarks:
JDAY 289, 0720z
Based on available forums, the possible payload for this launch is identified as either the  Qianfan Jigui 18A-I or Yaogan-40 04A-C
Source: https://forum.nasaspaceflight.com/index.php?topic=63684.0#msg2725257

Satellite Summaries:
The Qianfan constellation, also known as G60 or Thousand Sails, is an ambitious Chinese low-Earth orbit (LEO) broadband megaconstellation developed by Shanghai Spacecom Satellite Technology (SSST) under the Shanghai Yuanxin Satellite Technology Co.
Source: RC

The Yaogan-40 satellites represent a series of classified Chinese military reconnaissance spacecraft within the broader Yaogan (Remote Sensing) program, primarily designed for signals intelligence (SIGINT) and electromagnetic reconnaissance to monitor naval and electronic activities, though officially described by the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC) as conducting electromagnetic environment detection and related technical tests for scientific and remote sensing purposes.
Source: RC

JDAY 300, 0908Z

Mission Summary:
The payload for this launch has been confirmed to be the Gaofen-14-02, a topographic mapping satellite deployed to sun-sync orbit per official statements. It can obtain high precision stereo images globally, draw large scale digital topographic map, produce digital elevation models, digital surface models and digital orthophoto images, and provide basic geographic information. There are also suggestions that it may have a military-related mission.

The payload for this launch is speculated to be the Tianhui-3 02.

Tianhui-series Satellite Mission Summary:
The Tianhui-series satellites are part of China's Tianhui ("Sky Drawing") series of Earth observation and cartography satellites, with a primary mission to conduct high-resolution microwave surveying and mapping of the Earth's surface.  These satellites utilize L-band synthetic aperture radar (SAR) technology with an approximate 20-meter resolution, enabling all-weather, day-night imaging for applications to gather stereo data for the creation of precise, up-to-date, three-dimensional (3D) digital surface models and orthophotos for a variety of purposes, including geographic surveying, land resource management, scientific experiments, and potentially military-related applications due to the dual-use nature of the technology and the involvement of the People's Liberation Army (PLA) in the overall program contributing to China's expanding space-based electromagnetic environment experimentation and global surveillance network.
Source: RC

JDAY 300, 1545z

Mission Summary:
Shiyan-12-01 is a Chinese experimental/high-orbit satellite launched on 23 December 2021 aboard a Chang Zheng-7A (Long March 7A) rocket from Wenchang. It is one half of the twin Shiyan-12-01 / Shiyan-12-02 pair (codename HOTS  High Orbit Test Satellite) deployed to geosynchronous or near-geosynchronous orbit. Its publicized purpose is space environment studies and related technology demonstration; observers believe it may perform functions such as space weather monitoring, orbital calibration, drift-and-station-keeping tests, and possibly even inspection or rendezvousproximity operations (i.e., observing other GEO satellites). Its orbit is GEO drift / inclined GEO (~35,800 km altitude, small inclination), and its behavior (including periodic maneuvers and drift reversals) suggests its being used to test high-orbit satellite control, drift management, and possibly interactions or relative positioning with other satellites in GEO. 
Source: TRB

Mission Summary:
BD 3G (Beidou 3G) satellites are the GEO component of the 3rd phase of the Chinese Beidou (Compass) satellite navigation system, which, in contrast to GPS and GLONASS, uses both geostationary satellites and satellites in intermediate orbit.  This series, also called "Compass-G" is the geostationary constellation.  The satellites are based on the DFH-3B Bus.  They feature a phased array antenna for navigation signals and a laser retroreflector and additionally deployable S/L-band and C-band antennas.

JDay 300 at 2026z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified two maneuvers on Beidou 3G1 (43683) occurring on 26Oct1830z (JDay 299) and 27Oct1558z (JDay 300). 
 
During the first event, the satellite maneuvered from 140.2 deg E longitude with a delta-v of 27.62 m/s, resulting in an inclination change of -0.49 degs to a final inclination of 2.49 degs and a 5.1 dec increase in period. This maneuver appears to be a station-keeping maneuver and is within the historical pattern of life for this object. 

During the second event, the satellite maneuvered from 140.1 deg E longitude with a delta-v of 0.31 m/s, resulting in an increased period of 67.5 seconds which initiated a slight drift of -0.28 deg W/day. Based on this drift rate, we expect a period decrease maneuver to occur at perigee, approximately 2350z on 27Oct. This maneuver also appears to be a station-keeping maneuver and is within the historical pattern of life for this object. 

Of note, due to the west drift rate, Beidou 3G1 now has a close approach with SBIRS Geo 1 (53355) on 30Oct2015z at 26.6km and with Telstar 18V (43611) on 2Nov1856z at 21.5km. However, these close approaches will no longer be a factor following the expected future maneuver at 2350z.

Neighborhood of nearby objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver.

msgBody.Email_Subject: NOTSO - Photometric Change / SY-12-01 (50321) - 1aac_28Oct-0017Z - TACREP Notification
msgBody.Remarks:
JDAY 300, 1545z

Mission Summary:
Shiyan-12-01 is a Chinese experimental/high-orbit satellite launched on 23 December 2021 aboard a Chang Zheng-7A (Long March 7A) rocket from Wenchang. It is one half of the twin Shiyan-12-01 / Shiyan-12-02 pair (codename HOTS  High Orbit Test Satellite) deployed to geosynchronous or near-geosynchronous orbit. Its publicized purpose is space environment studies and related technology demonstration; observers believe it may perform functions such as space weather monitoring, orbital calibration, drift-and-station-keeping tests, and possibly even inspection or rendezvousproximity operations (i.e., observing other GEO satellites). Its orbit is GEO drift / inclined GEO (~35,800 km altitude, small inclination), and its behavior (including periodic maneuvers and drift reversals) suggests its being used to test high-orbit satellite control, drift management, and possibly interactions or relative positioning with other satellites in GEO. 
Source: TRB

JDAY 300, 1652z

Mission Summary:
BD 3G (Beidou 3G) satellites are the GEO component of the 3rd phase of the Chinese Beidou (Compass) satellite navigation system, which, in contrast to GPS and GLONASS, uses both geostationary satellites and satellites in intermediate orbit.  This series, also called "Compass-G" is the geostationary constellation.  The satellites are based on the DFH-3B Bus.  They feature a phased array antenna for navigation signals and a laser retroreflector and additionally deployable S/L-band and C-band antennas.
Source: https://space.skyrocket.de/doc_sdat/bd-3g.htm

JDay 301 at 1208z:
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers detected possible maneuver on Beidou 3G1 (43683) occurring at 0252z on 28Oct (JDay 301).
The satellite was located at 139.91 degs E longitude. Based off of initial indications it appears it is decreasing drift rate from 0.32 degs W/day to final 0.03 degs W/day and seems to be parking at 139.92 degs E long. Neighborhood of nearby objects is attached. 
No significant change in photometry is observed due to the maneuver.
Click link above to view products. Analysis is ongoing.

Beidou 3G1 (43683) is a Chinese satellite that supports government and commercial operations. The mission of Beidou 3G1 is satellite navigation.

JDay 300 at 2026z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified two maneuvers on Beidou 3G1 (43683) occurring on 26Oct1830z (JDay 299) and 27Oct1558z (JDay 300). 
 
During the first event, the satellite maneuvered from 140.2 deg E longitude with a delta-v of 27.62 m/s, resulting in an inclination change of -0.49 degs to a final inclination of 2.49 degs and a 5.1 dec increase in period. This maneuver appears to be a station-keeping maneuver and is within the historical pattern of life for this object. 

During the second event, the satellite maneuvered from 140.1 deg E longitude with a delta-v of 0.31 m/s, resulting in an increased period of 67.5 seconds which initiated a slight drift of -0.28 deg W/day. Based on this drift rate, we expect a period decrease maneuver to occur at perigee, approximately 2350z on 27Oct. This maneuver also appears to be a station-keeping maneuver and is within the historical pattern of life for this object. 

Of note, due to the west drift rate, Beidou 3G1 now has a close approach with SBIRS Geo 1 (53355) on 30Oct2015z at 26.6km and with Telstar 18V (43611) on 2Nov1856z at 21.5km. However, these close approaches will no longer be a factor following the expected future maneuver at 2350z.

Neighborhood of nearby objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver.

Mission Summary:
BD 3G (Beidou 3G) satellites are the GEO component of the 3rd phase of the Chinese Beidou (Compass) satellite navigation system, which, in contrast to GPS and GLONASS, uses both geostationary satellites and satellites in intermediate orbit.  This series, also called "Compass-G" is the geostationary constellation.  The satellites are based on the DFH-3B Bus.  They feature a phased array antenna for navigation signals and a laser retroreflector and additionally deployable S/L-band and C-band antennas.

JDAY 302, 2127z

Mission Summary:
Shiyan-12-01 is a Chinese experimental/high-orbit satellite launched on 23 December 2021 aboard a Chang Zheng-7A (Long March 7A) rocket from Wenchang. It is one half of the twin Shiyan-12-01 / Shiyan-12-02 pair (codename HOTS  High Orbit Test Satellite) deployed to geosynchronous or near-geosynchronous orbit. Its publicized purpose is space environment studies and related technology demonstration; observers believe it may perform functions such as space weather monitoring, orbital calibration, drift-and-station-keeping tests, and possibly even inspection or rendezvousproximity operations (i.e., observing other GEO satellites). Its orbit is GEO drift / inclined GEO (~35,800 km altitude, small inclination), and its behavior (including periodic maneuvers and drift reversals) suggests its being used to test high-orbit satellite control, drift management, and possibly interactions or relative positioning with other satellites in GEO. 
Source: EJS

Mission Summary:
Shiyan-12-01 is a Chinese experimental/high-orbit satellite launched on 23 December 2021 aboard a Chang Zheng-7A (Long March 7A) rocket from Wenchang. It is one half of the twin Shiyan-12-01 / Shiyan-12-02 pair (codename HOTS  High Orbit Test Satellite) deployed to geosynchronous or near-geosynchronous orbit. Its publicized purpose is space environment studies and related technology demonstration; observers believe it may perform functions such as space weather monitoring, orbital calibration, drift-and-station-keeping tests, and possibly even inspection or rendezvousproximity operations (i.e., observing other GEO satellites). Its orbit is GEO drift / inclined GEO (~35,800 km altitude, small inclination), and its behavior (including periodic maneuvers and drift reversals) suggests its being used to test high-orbit satellite control, drift management, and possibly interactions or relative positioning with other satellites in GEO. 
Source: EJS

JDAY 302, 2127z

Mission Summary:
Shiyan-12-01 is a Chinese experimental/high-orbit satellite launched on 23 December 2021 aboard a Chang Zheng-7A (Long March 7A) rocket from Wenchang. It is one half of the twin Shiyan-12-01 / Shiyan-12-02 pair (codename HOTS  High Orbit Test Satellite) deployed to geosynchronous or near-geosynchronous orbit. Its publicized purpose is space environment studies and related technology demonstration; observers believe it may perform functions such as space weather monitoring, orbital calibration, drift-and-station-keeping tests, and possibly even inspection or rendezvousproximity operations (i.e., observing other GEO satellites). Its orbit is GEO drift / inclined GEO (~35,800 km altitude, small inclination), and its behavior (including periodic maneuvers and drift reversals) suggests its being used to test high-orbit satellite control, drift management, and possibly interactions or relative positioning with other satellites in GEO. 
Source: EJS

Mission Summary:
Shiyan-12-01 is a Chinese experimental/high-orbit satellite launched on 23 December 2021 aboard a Chang Zheng-7A (Long March 7A) rocket from Wenchang. It is one half of the twin Shiyan-12-01 / Shiyan-12-02 pair (codename HOTS  High Orbit Test Satellite) deployed to geosynchronous or near-geosynchronous orbit. Its publicized purpose is space environment studies and related technology demonstration; observers believe it may perform functions such as space weather monitoring, orbital calibration, drift-and-station-keeping tests, and possibly even inspection or rendezvousproximity operations (i.e., observing other GEO satellites). Its orbit is GEO drift / inclined GEO (~35,800 km altitude, small inclination), and its behavior (including periodic maneuvers and drift reversals) suggests its being used to test high-orbit satellite control, drift management, and possibly interactions or relative positioning with other satellites in GEO.

JDay 304 at 1738z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified 2 maneuvers on OBJECT D (65547) occurring on 30 and 31 Oct.
The satellite maneuvered first on 1058z on J303 with a delta-V of 0.72 m/s resulting in an apogee of 797.15 km and a perigee of 769.46 km. The second maneuver was at 1027z on J304 with a delta-V of 2.67 m/s resulting in an apogee of 806.62 km and a perigee of 770.16 km. The purpose of this maneuver is unknown but it has slightly increased its eccentricity and period. Neighborhood is provided. Click link above to view products.

Object D (65547) is a CHN satellite associated with the launch of the LM-6A with the Yaogan-40 Group 03 A-C out of Taiyuan, China on 06 Sep 1634 UTC to LEO. Payload is not confirmed yet in Space-Track.org.
 
The specifics of the 1st maneuver are: 
--Time of Maneuver: 30 Oct 1058z
--Delta V: 0.72 m/s
--Period Change: 1.78 secs
--Apogee Change: 2.63 km
--Perigee Change: 0.2 km
--Inclination Change: 0.0 degs

The specifics of the 2nd maneuver are: 
--Time of Maneuver: 31 Oct 1027z
--Delta V: 2.67m/s
--Period Change: 6.44 secs
--Apogee Change: 9.45 km
--Perigee Change: 0.75 km

JDay 307 at 0100z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified 3rd maneuver on OBJECT D (65547) occurring on 1 Nov 2025.
The satellite maneuvered on 1240z with a delta-V of 4.40 m/s resulting in an apogee of 814.39 km and a perigee of 100.86 km. The purpose of this maneuver is unknown but it has slightly decreased its period and no changed in eccentricity. 

Object D (65547) is a CHN satellite associated with the launch of the LM-6A with the Yaogan-40 Group 03 A-C out of Taiyuan, China on 06 Sep 1634 UTC to LEO. Payload is not confirmed yet in Space-Track.org.

msgBody.Email_Subject: NOTSO - Maneuver / Luch Olymp 2 (55841) / GEO - aa5c_03Nov-1016Z - TACREP Notification
msgBody.Remarks:
JDAY 307, 1003Z

Mission Summary:
Luch 5X (OLYMP K-2) is a Russian geostationary satellite built for the Russian Ministry of Defense and the Russian intelligence agency, FSB. While the purpose of the satellites has not been officially disclosed, the satellites are believed to serve two purposes. The first purpose is to conduct signals intelligence (SIGINT) and the second is to provide secure communications lines for governmental use. The Luch designation, which is also used to refer to the Russian Satellite Data Relay Network (SDRN), hints at the satellites being used in a data relay role.
Source: TAB

JDay 307 at 1015z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers detected a possible maneuver on Luch (OLYMP) 2 (55841), occurring at 2142z on 02NOV2025 & JDAY306.

The satellite was located at 62.00 degs E longitude. Based off of initial indications it appears it is a SK Maneuver conducted in order to remain in the vicinity of INTELSAT 39 (44476). Click link above to view products. Analysis is ongoing.

LUCH (OLYMP) 2 (55841) is a Russian satellite that supports military operations. The mission of LUCH (OLYMP) 2 is to conduct Electronic Intelligence Operations to spy on communications satellites. It is also suspected of engaging in Russian espionage activities.

INTELSAT 39 (44476) is a US satellite that supports commercial operations. The mission of INTELSAT 39 is to provide high-throughput service, including broadband Internet and direct TV to Africa, Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and the Indian Ocean region.

JDay 307 at 1623z:

**This is a correction to the perigee from the previous NOTSO.**

 Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified 3rd maneuver on OBJECT D (65547) occurring on 1 Nov 2025.
The satellite maneuvered on 1240z with a delta-V of 4.40 m/s resulting in an apogee of 814.39 km and a perigee of 777.95 km. The purpose of this maneuver is unknown but it has slightly decreased its period and no changed in eccentricity. 

Object D (65547) is a CHN satellite associated with the launch of the LM-6A with the Yaogan-40 Group 03 A-C out of Taiyuan, China on 06 Sep 1634 UTC to LEO. Payload is not confirmed yet in Space-Track.org.
 
The specifics of the maneuver are: 
--Time of Maneuver: 1 Nov 1240z
--Delta V: 4.40 m/s
--Period Change: 9.85 secs
--Apogee Change: 7.72 km
--Perigee Change: 7.87 km
--Inclination Change: 0.0 degs

JDAY 307, 1809z

Mission Summary:
Luch Olymp-K is a Russian geostationary satellite built for the Russian Ministry of Defense and the Russian intelligence agency, FSB. Russian press reports indicate that the satellite may also be used by the Russian FSB for espionage and ELINT (including that of other satellites), in addition to Russian naval communications. During its first five years on orbit, Luch parked near more than a dozen commercial communications satellites for periods ranging from a few weeks to nine months, and typically close enough to be within the typical ground terminal uplink beam.

JDay 307 at 1845z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have an initial track for the unknown payload (94407) (possibly a YAOGAN-46). Based on current data, YAOGAN-46 is in a MEO transfer orbit, and appears to be a repeat of what happened with the YAOGAN-45 launch that occurred on 09SEP0200z from the Wenchang Satellite Launch Center, China. 
Object has an inclination of 20 degs and a RAAN of 117.79 degs.
Neighborhood is provided. Click link above to view products. 
 
YAOGAN-46 (94407) is a Chinese satellite that supports commercial operations. The mission of YAOGAN-46 is disaster prevention and mitigation, land resource surveys, and water conservancy and meteorological research.

JDay 307 at 1924z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified two maneuvers on the potential candidate for TJS-20 (66142) occurring on 31 Oct 1758z and 01 Nov 1930z. Object has an inclination of 5.98 degs and a RAAN of 300.49 degs.

The most recent maneuver occurred at 62.25 deg E longitude , with a delta-v of 1.55 m/s, resulting in a decrease in eastward drift rate from 0.11 E deg/day to 0.01 W deg/day indicating that it has parked.

TJS-20 candidate parked in-between and is plane matched with:
- ABS 4 (28184) at 61.13 deg Longitude and 5.46 deg Inclination.
- INTEL SAT 906 (27513) at 64.31 deg Longitude and 5.22 deg Inclination.

Neighborhood is provided.  Click link above to view products.

TJS-20 (66142) is a Chinese satellite that supports unknown operations and with an unknown mission.

msgBody.Remarks:
JDAY 307, 2005z

Mission Summary:
Shijian-23 (catalog number 55131, international designation 2023-002A), launched by China on January 9, 2023, aboard a Long March 7A rocket from the Wenchang Satellite Launch Center, represents a key mission in the nation's Shijian experimental satellite series aimed at advancing space technology and scientific research. As part of this classified program, the satellite was deployed into a geostationary transfer orbit, from which it utilized onboard propulsion to reach geosynchronous orbit, enabling extended operations for up to 15 years based on the DFH-4E satellite bus platform. Its primary objectives encompass conducting undisclosed scientific experiments and verifying advanced technical capabilities, potentially including innovations in communications, space environment monitoring, or rendezvous and proximity operations, consistent with the series' historical focus on practical applications for future missions like those in the China High-resolution Earth Observation System (CHEOS).
Source: EJS

Mission Summary:
Shijian-23 (catalog number 55131, international designation 2023-002A), launched by China on January 9, 2023, aboard a Long March 7A rocket from the Wenchang Satellite Launch Center, represents a key mission in the nation's Shijian experimental satellite series aimed at advancing space technology and scientific research. As part of this classified program, the satellite was deployed into a geostationary transfer orbit, from which it utilized onboard propulsion to reach geosynchronous orbit, enabling extended operations for up to 15 years based on the DFH-4E satellite bus platform. Its primary objectives encompass conducting undisclosed scientific experiments and verifying advanced technical capabilities, potentially including innovations in communications, space environment monitoring, or rendezvous and proximity operations, consistent with the series' historical focus on practical applications for future missions like those in the China High-resolution Earth Observation System (CHEOS).
Source: EJS

JDay 307 at 2300z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a maneuver on Luch (OLYMP) 2 (55841) occurring at 2301z on 02 Nov on JDAY 306. 

The satellite maneuvered from 62.03 degs E longitude with a delta-v of 0.15 m/s, resulting in an increased east drift rate by 0.0026 deg/day to 0.0046 E deg/day. Based off of indications it appears it is perched in the vicinity of INTELSAT 39 (44476) and is drifting away by ~7kms per day.  Neighborhood of nearby objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver.
 
LUCH (OLYMP) 2 (55841) is a Russian satellite that supports military operations. The mission of LUCH (OLYMP) 2 is to conduct Electronic Intelligence Operations to spy on communications satellites. It is also suspected of engaging in Russian espionage activities.

INTELSAT 39 (44476) is a US satellite that supports commercial operations. The mission of INTELSAT 39 is to provide high-throughput service, including broadband Internet and direct TV to Africa, Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and the Indian Ocean region.

msgBody.Remarks:
Band info for SPAINSAT NG II:

The new Spainsat NG generation will multiply by 16 times the capacity in X and Ka military band with respect to the current devices and will add a new payload in UHF band. In addition, it will operate with active X-band antennas in receive and transmit. Pioneers in the European aerospace sector, each of them will be assigned 16 different areas of operation to perform their coverage services with electronic configuration.

Source: https://nextspaceflight.com/launches/details/7046/

Band info for CMS-03 satellite (GSAT-7R):

The satellite, which costs around Rs 1,589 crore, uses multiple frequency bands, including UHF, S, C, and Ku bands, allowing it to send voice, video, and data. This will enable seamless communication between naval ships, submarines, and aircraft spread across the Indian Ocean Region, covering up to 2,000 km from India's coastline.

Source: https://www.theweek.in/news/defence/2025/10/21/cms-02-satellite-launch-likely-in-november-why-this-is-a-major-upgrade-for-indian-navys-operations-maritime-defence.html

JDay 310 at 1945z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have indications of an uncorrelated track (UCT) in GEO at 92.1 deg E Longitude at 1814z. The satellite could potentially be SPAINSAT NG II or CMS-03 (GSAT-7R). Click link above to view products.
 
 Observation and effort to identify the object is ongoing.
 
 Close approaches within window: None
 Current longitude: 92.1 deg E (over eastern Indian Ocean by Malaysia and Indonesia)
 Current drift rate: 0.27 W/day
 RAAN: 271.39
 Inc: 0.23
 VisMag Range: approx 8.8 to 12
 
SPAINSAT NG II is a Spanish satellite that supports military operations. The mission of SPAINSAT NG II is a tri-band (UHF, X, Ka) satellite built by an Airbus-led consortium for Hisdesat, serving the Spanish Ministry of Defense and its allies. It is hardened against interference and nuclear events.
 
CMS-03 (GSAT-7R) is a Indian satellite that supports Navy military operations. The mission of CMS-03 is a secure multi-band (UHF, S, C, Ku) communication satellite that replaced the older GSAT-7 Rukmini.

JDay 310 at 2330z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a maneuver on OBJECT D (65547) occurring at 1751z on 05 Nov (JDAY308).

The satellite maneuvered with a delta v of 4.54 m/s, resulting in an increase of apogee to 834.36km and perigee to 828.34 km. This appears as a follow on manoeuvre to the one observed on JDay 307 as reported in previous NOTSO (id: a923)

No blue satellites within immediate neighbourhood (see attached products)
 
OBJECT D (65547) is a PRC satellite associated with the launch of the LM-6A with the Yaogan-40 Group 03 A-C out of Taiyuan, China on 06 Sep 1634 UTC to LEO. Payload is not yet confirmed in Space-Track.

--Time of Maneuver: 05NOV 1751z
--Delta V: 3.13 m/s
--Period Change: 11.4 secs

msgBody.Remarks:
7 Nov JDAY 311, 0612UTC

Gaofen 13, an improved version of Gaofen 4 is a Chinese civilian remote sensing satellite for the state-sponsored program CHEOS (China High resolution Earth Observation System). There is speculation as to the military purpose of the Gaofen-13 which China reports as 'wild' speculation. Possible Chinese military applications include identifying and tracking U.S. Strike Carrier Group activities, particularly in the SCS. There is also speculation as to the possibly missile warning purpose of the satellite. The Gaofen-13 is suspected to be an improved version of the Gaofen-4 satellite with significantly larger optical systems. 
<Sourced by JB from SatelliteDossier>

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers detected a possible maneuver on GAOFEN 13 (46610), occurring at 1838z on 06NOV25 (JDAY310).

msgBody.Event_Description:
JDay 311 at 1101z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers detected a possible maneuver on OBJECT D (65547), occurring at 1151 on 06NOV25 & JDAY 310.

First indications suggest, that the satellite maneuvered with a delta-v of 4.61m/s, resulting in an increase of apogee to 849.22 km and perigee to 831.34 km. 
This appears as a follow on maneuver to the last maneuver observed at 1751z on 05 Nov (JDAY 309) as reported in previous NOTSO. 
Click link above to view products. Analysis is ongoing.

OBJECT D (65547) is a PRC satellite associated with the launch of the LM-6A with the Yaogan-40 Group 03 A-C out of Taiyuan, China on 06 Sep 1634 UTC to LEO. Payload is not yet confirmed in Space-Track.

msgBody.Remarks:
7 Nov JDAY 311, 0612UTC

Gaofen 13, an improved version of Gaofen 4 is a Chinese civilian remote sensing satellite for the state-sponsored program CHEOS (China High resolution Earth Observation System). There is speculation as to the military purpose of the Gaofen-13 which China reports as 'wild' speculation. Possible Chinese military applications include identifying and tracking U.S. Strike Carrier Group activities, particularly in the SCS. There is also speculation as to the possibly missile warning purpose of the satellite. The Gaofen-13 is suspected to be an improved version of the Gaofen-4 satellite with significantly larger optical systems. 
<Sourced by JB from SatelliteDossier>

JDay 311 at 1248z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a maneuver on GAOFEN 13 (46610) occurring at 1814z on 06NOV25 & JDAY 310.
The satellite maneuvered from 117.77 deg E longitude with a delta-v of 7.76 m/s, resulting in the initiation of an eastward drift with a drift rate of 0.007 deg E/day, an inclination change of 0.066 degs to a final inclination of 0.083 degs and decreased period change of 2.61 sec. This maneuver appears to be a station-keeping maneuver and is within the historical pattern of life for this object. 
Neighborhood of nearby objects is attached showing no upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver. Click link above to view products.

GAOFEN 13 (46610) is a PRC satellite that supports civil operations. The mission of GAOFEN 13 is Earth Observation/Imaging (<5m res).

--Time of Maneuver: 06NOV1814z

Band info for SPAINSAT NG II:

The new Spainsat NG generation will multiply by 16 times the capacity in X and Ka military band with respect to the current devices and will add a new payload in UHF band. In addition, it will operate with active X-band antennas in receive and transmit. Pioneers in the European aerospace sector, each of them will be assigned 16 different areas of operation to perform their coverage services with electronic configuration.

Source: https://nextspaceflight.com/launches/details/7046/

Band info for CMS-03 satellite (GSAT-7R):

The satellite, which costs around Rs 1,589 crore, uses multiple frequency bands, including UHF, S, C, and Ku bands, allowing it to send voice, video, and data. This will enable seamless communication between naval ships, submarines, and aircraft spread across the Indian Ocean Region, covering up to 2,000 km from India's coastline.

Source: https://www.theweek.in/news/defence/2025/10/21/cms-02-satellite-launch-likely-in-november-why-this-is-a-major-upgrade-for-indian-navys-operations-maritime-defence.html

JDay 311 at 1735z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers detected a possible maneuver on a newly discovered UCT in GEO at 91.7 deg E Longitude at 7Nov1357z (JDay 311).  The satellite was located at 91.7 degs E longitude. Based off of initial indications it appears it reversed its drift of 0.28 deg W/day to 1.3 deg E/day with an unknown destination. 

The satellite could potentially be SPAINSAT NG II or CMS-03 (GSAT-7R). Of note, CMS-2 (52903) performed initial checkout at 93.5 deg E. Click link above to view products. 

SPAINSAT NG II is a Spanish satellite that supports military operations. The mission of SPAINSAT NG II is a tri-band (UHF, X, Ka) satellite built by an Airbus-led consortium for Hisdesat, serving the Spanish Ministry of Defense and its allies. It is hardened against interference and nuclear events.
 
CMS-03 (GSAT-7R) is a Indian satellite that supports Navy military operations. The mission of CMS-03 is a secure multi-band (UHF, S, C, Ku) communication satellite that replaced the older GSAT-7 Rukmini.

JDay 311 at 1815z:

msgBody.Remarks:
Band info for SPAINSAT NG II:

The new Spainsat NG generation will multiply by 16 times the capacity in X and Ka military band with respect to the current devices and will add a new payload in UHF band. In addition, it will operate with active X-band antennas in receive and transmit. Pioneers in the European aerospace sector, each of them will be assigned 16 different areas of operation to perform their coverage services with electronic configuration.

Source: https://nextspaceflight.com/launches/details/7046/

Band info for CMS-03 satellite (GSAT-7R):

The satellite, which costs around Rs 1,589 crore, uses multiple frequency bands, including UHF, S, C, and Ku bands, allowing it to send voice, video, and data. This will enable seamless communication between naval ships, submarines, and aircraft spread across the Indian Ocean Region, covering up to 2,000 km from India's coastline.

Source: https://www.theweek.in/news/defence/2025/10/21/cms-02-satellite-launch-likely-in-november-why-this-is-a-major-upgrade-for-indian-navys-operations-maritime-defence.html

JDay 311 at 1830z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a maneuver on the newly-discovered UCT occurring 07Nov1357z.

The satellite maneuvered from 91.87deg E longitude with a delta-v of 4.88 m/s, resulting in a reversal of drift direction from 0.26 W deg/day to 1.40 E deg/day, and a period change of -399.51sec to a final period of 1430.54min. This maneuver does not appear to be a station-keeping maneuver. Neighborhood of nearby objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver.

The satellite could potentially be SPAINSAT NG II or CMS-03 (GSAT-7R). 
Of note, CMS-02 (52903) performed initial checkout at 93.5 deg E and if this is CMS-03, it might be performing a checkout at the same location. Click link above to view products. 

SPAINSAT NG II is a Spanish satellite that supports military operations. The mission of SPAINSAT NG II is a tri-band (UHF, X, Ka) satellite built by an Airbus-led consortium for Hisdesat, serving the Spanish Ministry of Defense and its allies. It is hardened against interference and nuclear events.

CMS-03 (GSAT-7R) is a Indian satellite that supports Navy military operations. The mission of CMS-03 is a secure multi-band (UHF, S, C, Ku) communication satellite that replaced the older GSAT-7 Rukmini.

The specifics of the maneuver are: 
--Time of Maneuver: 07Nov1357z
--Delta V: 4.88 m/s

--Apogee Change: -197.59 km

Band info for SPAINSAT NG II:

The new Spainsat NG generation will multiply by 16 times the capacity in X and Ka military band with respect to the current devices and will add a new payload in UHF band. In addition, it will operate with active X-band antennas in receive and transmit. Pioneers in the European aerospace sector, each of them will be assigned 16 different areas of operation to perform their coverage services with electronic configuration.

Source: https://nextspaceflight.com/launches/details/7046/

Band info for CMS-03 satellite (GSAT-7R):

The satellite, which costs around Rs 1,589 crore, uses multiple frequency bands, including UHF, S, C, and Ku bands, allowing it to send voice, video, and data. This will enable seamless communication between naval ships, submarines, and aircraft spread across the Indian Ocean Region, covering up to 2,000 km from India's coastline.

Source: https://www.theweek.in/news/defence/2025/10/21/cms-02-satellite-launch-likely-in-november-why-this-is-a-major-upgrade-for-indian-navys-operations-maritime-defence.html

JDay 311 at 2030z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, for the UCT discovered at 92 E longitude, JCO providers detected a verified maneuver on 07Nov1803z, afterwards the UCT appeared unstable 07Nov1826z and then appeared stable again on 07Nov2011z. While it was unstable there appears to be a possible maneuver on 07Nov1950z before the UCT regained stability.  Will note that the UCT appeared to go stable around the time it entered solar exclusion. Analysis is on-going.

The photometric changes occurred between the solar phase angles of 10 to 35 from 07Nov1826z to 07Nov2011z. The 1st change occurred ~07Nov1826z and the 2nd change occurred ~07Nov2011z. 

The UCT maneuvered with a delta-v of 0.27 m/s, resulting in a period change of +20.36sec decreasing the drift from 1.4 E deg/day to 1.32 E deg/day . This maneuver does not appear to be a station-keeping maneuver. Neighborhood of nearby objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver. Analysis is ongoing.

The UCT could potentially be SPAINSAT NG II or CMS-03 (GSAT-7R). 

Note: CMS-02 (52903) performed initial checkout at 93.5 deg E and if this is CMS-03, it might be performing a checkout at the same location. Click link above to view products.

SPAINSAT NG II is a Spanish satellite that supports military operations. The mission of SPAINSAT NG II is a tri-band (UHF, X, Ka) satellite built by an Airbus-led consortium for Hisdesat, serving the Spanish Ministry of Defense and its allies. It is hardened against interference and nuclear events.

CMS-03 (GSAT-7R) is a Indian satellite that supports Navy military operations. The mission of CMS-03 is a secure multi-band (UHF, S, C, Ku) communication satellite that replaced the older GSAT-7 Rukmini.

JDay 311 at 2000z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers verified a maneuver on SY-12-02 (50322), occurring at 0525z on 7 Nov & JDAY 311.

The satellite maneuvered from 106 deg E longitude with a delta-v of 0.13 m/s, resulting in a decrease in westward drift rate, period change of +7.03 seconds, apogee change of +2.56 km, and perigee change of+2.02 km.  This maneuver appears to have been to increase the separate distance between 50322 and well-tracked UCT 71051 from close approach of 29 km to 48 km and is within the historical pattern of life for this object. Neighborhood of nearby objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuver.

SHIYAN 12-02 (50322) is a Chinese satellite that supports military operations. The mission of SY-12-02 is officially for space environment exploration and related technology tests however, it is suspected that it is actually a military test satellite.

JDAY 313, 1812Z

Mission Summary:
The Chutian-2 01-02 satellites are technology demonstration satellites mainly used to conduct optical remote sensing observation experiments.  After entering orbit, they will verify the satellite's Earth observation capabilities and super-resolution processing application capabilities. The satellite data will be mainly applied in areas such as the safe operation and maintenance of large-scale water conservancy facilities, dynamic monitoring of the marine ecological environment, natural disaster prediction and early warning, and disaster assessment.

JDay 314 at 0243z:
 
Based on available PAIR data, JCO providers have indications of successful launch of a LM-12 from Wenchang, China on 10 Nov occurring at 0243z, carrying an unknown payload but could possibly be GuoWang SatNet 13 series A-I (aka Xingwang Digui). Based on current information, the satellite is likely to be LEO with orbital characteristics of 50deg Inc and 39deg RAAN. COCO is provided. Neighborhood is provided. JDay 314 at 0131z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified three maneuvers on Object D (65547) occurring between 1055z 07 Nov and 1533z 09 Nov.

The satellite maneuvered with a total delta v of 4.82 m/s, resulting in a total increase of its perigee by 12.77km and total increase of its period by 10.16 seconds. Object D looks to be moving into the vicinity of Objects B (65545) and C (65556) which are part of the same Yaogan 40-03 Group. COCO is provided showing near plane match with Object B and C. Click link above to view products.
 
Object D (65547) is a Chinese satellite that supports military operations. 
Mission Summary (PAIR):
Per official sources this is part of the Yaogan 40-03 Group (Remote Sensing Satellite Group 40, Group 03). It's mission is described as "to conduct electromagnetic environment monitoring and related technical testing".
 
The aggregate result of the maneuvers are: 
--Time of Maneuvers: Between 1055z 07 Nov and 1533z 09 Nov
--Delta V: 4.82 m/s
--Period Change: 10.16 secs
--Apogee Change: 3.91 km
--Perigee Change: 12.77 km
--Inclination Change: 0.01 degs

Individual maneuver results are in the attached products.

JDay 311 at 1815z:

Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified a maneuver on OBJECT D (65547) occurring 06Nov1204z.

The satellite maneuvered with a delta v of 4.23 m/s, resulting in a +11.17sec period change resulting in a final period of 101.78min. It appears OBJECT D (65547) is joining up with OBJECT C (65546) and OBJECT B (65545) which are at a 101.95min period. OBJECT A (65544) and OBJECT E (65548) are paired up at a ~100.93min period. This maneuver does not appear to be a station-keeping maneuver and is not within the historical pattern of life for this object. Neighborhood is provided. Click link above to view products.

OBJECT D (65547) is a PRC satellite associated with the launch of the LM-6A with the Yaogan-40 Group 03 A-C out of Taiyuan, China on 06 Sep 1634 UTC to LEO. Payload is not yet confirmed in Space-Track.

JDay 314 at 0400z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have an updated track for the possible Yaogan-46 (63313) which launched 3 Nov from Wenchang, China. 
Orbital characteristics are an inclination of 20.02 deg and RAAN of 112.97 deg and it appears that YAOGAN-46 is in a MEO orbit which is showing indications of being circularized.
 
YAOGAN-46 (94407) is a Chinese satellite that supports commercial operations. The mission of YAOGAN-46 is disaster prevention and mitigation, land resource surveys, and water conservancy and meteorological research.

Click link above to view products.

Based on current data, YAOGAN-46 is in a MEO transfer orbit, and appears to be a repeat of what happened with the YAOGAN-45 launch that occurred on 09SEP0200z from the Wenchang Satellite Launch Center, China. 
Object has an inclination of 20 degs and a RAAN of 117.79 degs.
Neighborhood is provided. Click link above to view products. 
 
YAOGAN-46 (94407) is a Chinese satellite that supports commercial operations. The mission of YAOGAN-46 is disaster prevention and mitigation, land resource surveys, and water conservancy and meteorological research.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------JDay 307 at 0530z:
 
Based on available PAIR data, JCO providers have indications of a successful launch of a LM-7A from Wenchang, China, occurring at 0347z on JDay307, carrying an unknown payload (possibly a DFH-4 bus, a telecommunications satellite platform). Based on current information, the satellite is likely to be GEO.
The TLEs for the satellites and rocket body are currently still being defined. Analysis is ongoing. 

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

JDay 304 at 1750z:
 
Based on available PAIR data, JCO providers have received indications of a possible upcoming launch of a LM-7A from Wenchang, China on the 3rd of November with a launch window of 0339z to 0402z with an expected launch time of 0347z, carrying an unknown payload (possibly a DFH-4 bus, a telecommunications satellite platform). Based on current information, the satellite is likely to be GEO.

Click link above to view products.

JCO expects that it will launch into a 19 deg inclination and then at the first nodal crossing will change to 15.5 degs.  TLEs have been provided for both inclinations.

msgBody.Remarks:
Band info for SPAINSAT NG II:

The new Spainsat NG generation will multiply by 16 times the capacity in X and Ka military band with respect to the current devices and will add a new payload in UHF band. In addition, it will operate with active X-band antennas in receive and transmit. Pioneers in the European aerospace sector, each of them will be assigned 16 different areas of operation to perform their coverage services with electronic configuration.

Source: https://nextspaceflight.com/launches/details/7046/

Band info for CMS-03 satellite (GSAT-7R):

The satellite, which costs around Rs 1,589 crore, uses multiple frequency bands, including UHF, S, C, and Ku bands, allowing it to send voice, video, and data. This will enable seamless communication between naval ships, submarines, and aircraft spread across the Indian Ocean Region, covering up to 2,000 km from India's coastline.

Source: https://www.theweek.in/news/defence/2025/10/21/cms-02-satellite-launch-likely-in-november-why-this-is-a-major-upgrade-for-indian-navys-operations-maritime-defence.html

JDay 314 at 0410z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have verified 3 maneuvers on the newly-discovered UCT occurring between 07 Nov 21:28 UTC and 09 Nov 05:01 UTC.

The satellite maneuvered from 91.6 deg E longitude with a delta-v of 4.02m/s, resulting in arresting eastward drift and parking at 93.5 deg E, and a period change of +318.64 sec. This maneuvers does not appear to be a station-keeping maneuver.

Neighborhood of nearby objects is attached showing upcoming close approaches as a result of this maneuvers. Notably, the satellites current position shows colocation with GSAT 15 (41028) and GSAT 17 (42815).

CMS-02 (GSAT-24) (52903) performed initial checkout at 93.5 deg E. If this new object is indeed the recently launched CMS-03 (GSAT-7R), it may be undergoing a similar checkout process at the same location.

CMS-03 (GSAT-7R) is an Indian satellite that supports Navy military operations. The mission of CMS-03 is a secure multi-band (UHF, S, C, Ku) communication satellite that replaced the older GSAT-7 Rukmini.

The specifics of the maneuver are: 
--Time of Maneuver: 07 Nov 21:28 UTC and 09 Nov 05:01 UTC
--Delta V: 4.02 m/s
--Period Change: +318.64 sec
--Apogee Change: +93.266 km
--Perigee Change: +114.76 km
--Inclination Change: 0.0013 degs

Mission Summary:  
 Shijian 23, or SJ-23, (SAT ID 55131) is a Chinese experimental and "technical verification" satellite known for RPO activity along the GEO belt. Originally launched 8 Jan 2023, it reached the GEO belt on 15 Jan 23 and was released from the Apogee Kick Motor (AKM). It is built on the DongFangHong-4E bus and uses chemical and possibly electric propulsion.

JDay 314 at 1050z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have detected a Photometric change on SJ-23 (55131). This change occurred between the solar phase angles of 17.2 to 44.7 and appeared to be ~1 visual magnitude dimmer. 
 
The cause of the change may be associated with past close approach with 
SPAINSAT NG1 (62852) at 09NOV2344z at 90.62 km; with bad lighting
RADUGA 1M-3 (39375) at 09NOV2248z at 97.32 km; with bad lighting

SJ-23 also have future close approaches with
RADUGA 3 (10159) at 10NOV1935z at 97.65 km; with good lighting
EUTE 36D (59346) at 10NOV2339z at 70.74 km; with bad lighting
EXPRESS AMU1 (41191) at 10NOV2339z at 137.6 km; with bad lighting

This photometric variation is not consistent with the historical pattern of life for this object. Analysis is ongoing.
 
The satellite is in GEO and is currently at 35.5 degs E longitude and is drifting at 0.74 E deg/day. Neighborhood is provided. Click link above to view products

JDay 314  at1100z:

Based on available PAIR data, JCO providers have indications of an unsuccessful launch in to orbit of a Ceres-1 from Jiuquan, China after a successful lift off  on 10 NOV 2025 occurring at  0402z, carrying North University of China Satellite 1. Source indicates first, second, and third stages had functional operation. However 510 seconds after the fourth stage ignition, an anomaly occurred resulting in a premature shutdown and failure to deliver the satellite into orbit. Mission Summary:  
 Shijian 23, or SJ-23, (SAT ID 55131) is a Chinese experimental and "technical verification" satellite known for RPO activity along the GEO belt. Originally launched 8 Jan 2023, it reached the GEO belt on 15 Jan 23 and was released from the Apogee Kick Motor (AKM). It is built on the DongFangHong-4E bus and uses chemical and possibly electric propulsion.

Band info for SPAINSAT NG II:

The new Spainsat NG generation will multiply by 16 times the capacity in X and Ka military band with respect to the current devices and will add a new payload in UHF band. In addition, it will operate with active X-band antennas in receive and transmit. Pioneers in the European aerospace sector, each of them will be assigned 16 different areas of operation to perform their coverage services with electronic configuration.

Source: https://nextspaceflight.com/launches/details/7046/

Band info for CMS-03 satellite (GSAT-7R):

The satellite, which costs around Rs 1,589 crore, uses multiple frequency bands, including UHF, S, C, and Ku bands, allowing it to send voice, video, and data. This will enable seamless communication between naval ships, submarines, and aircraft spread across the Indian Ocean Region, covering up to 2,000 km from India's coastline.

Source: https://www.theweek.in/news/defence/2025/10/21/cms-02-satellite-launch-likely-in-november-why-this-is-a-major-upgrade-for-indian-navys-operations-maritime-defence.html

JDay 316 at 2121z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers have detected 2 verified maneuvers by COSMOS 2590 (64527, occurring 10Nov ~0821z and 12Nov ~1258z. This satellite is currently in an RPO with COSMOS 258 (64467), which it was deployed from. 

Prior to the maneuvers they were in an RPO with a RIC of [3 x -3 x 20]. The maneuver on 10Nov0820z tightened up the conditions of the RPO, bringing all RIC values within 10km [3 x 10 x 8km]. These conditions existed for a little under 2 days where we saw a close approach of 230 meters. The most recent maneuver on 12Nov1258z earlier today has separation on the negative in track at about 9km a day. and separation on the radial of ~3km a day.

The TRIC plot will show the new relative motion. Click link above to view products.
 
The specifics of the 1st maneuver are: 
--Time of Maneuver: 10Nov0821z
--Delta V: 0.73 m/s
--Period Change: +0.9 secs
--Apogee Change: -3.57 km
--Perigee Change: +.14 km
--Inclination Change: -0.03 degs
 
The specifics of the 2nd maneuver are: 
--Time of Maneuver: 12Nov1258z
--Delta V: 0.8 m/s
--Period Change: +3.07 secs
--Apogee Change: -5.88 km
--Perigee Change: +7.89 km
--Inclination Change: +0.0115 degs

JDay 317 at 0835z:
 
Based on current SDA observations and available PAIR data, JCO providers detected a possible a 3rd maneuver by COSMOS 2590 (64527), occurring 12Nov ~1809z. This satellite is currently in an RPO with COSMOS 2589 (64467), which it was deployed from. The TRIC plot does indicate a gradual increasing separation between the objects, however it is too early to determine whether another maneuver will occur to reduce RIC distances, or whether there will be a continued increase in separation between the two objects.

The satellites are IVO 108.38deg E longitude. The maneuver had a delta v of 2.12 m/s, the effect of which was 0.035 decrease in westward drift rate however, awaiting verification. The TRIC plot will show the new relative motion. Click link above to view products.

Mission Summary:
AsiaSat 7 is a Hong Kong communications satellite, which is operated by the Hong Kongbased Asia Satellite Telecommunications Company (AsiaSat). It is positioned in geostationary orbit at a longitude of 105 East of the Greenwich Meridian, where it serves as a back-up for the AsiaSat 5 satellite and replaced AsiaSat 3S. It is used to provide fixed satellite services, including broadcasting, telephone and broadband very small aperture terminal (VSAT) communications, to Asia and the Pacific Ocean region. The satellite has 28 C-band and 17 Ku-band transponders and a Ka-band payload. Its region-wide high power C-band beam covers Asia, the Middle East, Australasia and Central Asia, with Ku-band beams serving East Asia, South Asia and a steerable Ku beam.
Source: TRB
